docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text: ಯದೇವೇಹ ತದಮುತ್ರ ಯದಮುತ್ರ ತದನ್ವಿಹ । ಮೃತ್ಯೋಃ ಸ ಮೃತ್ಯುಮಾಪ್ನೋತಿ ಯ ಇಹ ನಾನೇವ ಪಶ್ಯತಿ ॥ ೧೦ ॥   Whatever is here, that indeed is there; and whatever is there, that indeed is here. He who sees even the slightest plurality here goes from death to death.

docs.text:
ಯತ್ ಏವ ಇಹ

Whatever indeed is here

ತತ್ ಅಮುತ್ರ

That is there

  • ತತ್ → that
  • ಅಮುತ್ರ → there

ಯತ್ ಅಮುತ್ರ

Whatever is there

ತತ್ ಅನು ಇಹ

  • ಇಹ → here

ಮೃತ್ಯೋಃ ಸಃ ಮೃತ್ಯುಂ ಆಪ್ನೋತಿ

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಮೃತ್ಯುಂ → death
  • ಆಪ್ನೋತಿ → attains

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text: ಯದ್ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಾದಿಸ್ಥಾವರಾಂತೇಷು ವರ್ತಮಾನಂ ತತ್ತದುಪಾಧಿತ್ವಾದಬ್ರಹ್ಮವದವಭಾಸಮಾನಂ ಸಂಸಾರ್ಯನ್ಯತ್ಪರಸ್ಮಾದ್ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣ ಇತಿ ಮಾ ಭೂತ್ಕಸ್ಯಚಿದಾಶಂಕೇತೀದಮಾಹ — ಯದೇವೇಹ ಕಾರ್ಯಕಾರಣೋಪಾಧಿಸಮನ್ವಿತಂ ಸಂಸಾರಧರ್ಮವದವಭಾಸಮಾನಮವಿವೇಕಿನಾಮ್ , ತದೇವ ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮಸ್ಥಮ್ ಅಮುತ್ರ ನಿತ್ಯವಿಜ್ಞಾನಘನಸ್ವಭಾವಂ ಸರ್ವಸಂಸಾರಧರ್ಮವರ್ಜಿತಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ । ಯಚ್ಚ ಅಮುತ್ರ ಅಮುಷ್ಮಿನ್ನಾತ್ಮನಿ ಸ್ಥಿತಮ್ , ತದನು ಇಹ ತದೇವ ಇಹ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರಣನಾಮರೂಪೋಪಾಧಿಮ್ ಅನು ವಿಭಾವ್ಯಮಾನಂ ನಾನ್ಯತ್ । ತತ್ರೈವಂ ಸತಿ ಉಪಾಧಿಸ್ವಭಾವಭೇದದೃಷ್ಟಿಲಕ್ಷಣಯಾ ಅವಿದ್ಯಯಾ ಮೋಹಿತಃ ಸನ್ ಯ ಇಹ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣ್ಯನಾನಾಭೂತೇ ಪರಸ್ಮಾದನ್ಯೋಽಹಂ ಮತ್ತೋಽನ್ಯತ್ಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮೇತಿ ನಾನೇವ ಭಿನ್ನಮಿವ ಪಶ್ಯತಿ ಉಪಲಭತೇ, ಸ ಮೃತ್ಯೋರ್ಮರಣಾತ್ ಮೃತ್ಯುಂ ಮರಣಂ ಪುನಃ ಪುನಃ ಜನನಮರಣಭಾವಮಾಪ್ನೋತಿ ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯತೇ । ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ತಥಾ ನ ಪಶ್ಯೇತ್ । ವಿಜ್ಞಾನೈಕರಸಂ ನೈರಂತರ್ಯೇಣಾಕಾಶವತ್ಪರಿಪೂರ್ಣಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮೈವಾಹಮಸ್ಮೀತಿ ಪಶ್ಯೇದಿತಿ ವಾಕ್ಯಾರ್ಥಃ ॥   Lest anyone entertain the doubt that the Self appearing in all beings—from Brahmā down to the smallest stationary object—is something different from the Supreme Brahman because it appears conditioned and subject to saṃsāra, the Upaniṣad declares this mantra.  That which appears here to the undiscriminating as associated with causes, effects, and limiting adjuncts, and therefore as possessing the characteristics of worldly existence, is itself the very Brahman that exists in its own nature, there (in reality), as pure consciousness, eternal, homogeneous knowledge, and free from all attributes of saṃsāra.  And that which exists there in the Self is precisely what appears here through the adjuncts of body, senses, names, and forms. It is not something different.  When this is so, a person deluded by ignorance, characterized by perceiving differences arising from limiting adjuncts, imagines:  "I am different from Brahman; Brahman is something other than me."  Seeing plurality as though it were real, he repeatedly attains death—that is, repeated birth and death.  Therefore one should not see in that manner.  Rather, one should realize:  "I am Brahman alone—of the nature of pure consciousness, continuous, and all-pervading like space."  This is the meaning of the passage.

ಯತ್ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಾದಿ ಸ್ಥಾವರಾಂತೇಷು ವರ್ತಮಾನಂ

That which exists in all beings from Brahmā down to the immobile

  • ಯತ್ → that which
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಾದಿ → beginning with Brahmā
  • ಸ್ಥಾವರಾಂತೇಷು → ending with stationary beings
  • ವರ್ತಮಾನಂ → existing

ತತ್ ತತ್ ಉಪಾಧಿತ್ವಾತ್

Because of various limiting adjuncts

  • ತತ್ ತತ್ → various
  • ಉಪಾಧಿತ್ವಾತ್ → due to conditioning adjuncts

ಅಬ್ರಹ್ಮವತ್ ಅವಭಾಸಮಾನಂ

Appearing as though non-Brahman

  • ಅಬ್ರಹ್ಮವತ್ → as though not Brahman
  • ಅವಭಾಸಮಾನಂ → appearing

ಸಂಸಾರಿ ಅನ್ಯತ್ ಪರಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಃ

Something different from the Supreme Brahman and subject to saṃsāra

  • ಸಂಸಾರಿ → worldly, transmigrating
  • ಅನ್ಯತ್ → different
  • ಪರಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಃ → from Supreme Brahman

ಮಾ ಭೂತ್ ಕಸ್ಯಚಿತ್ ಆಶಂಕಾ

Lest anyone have such a doubt

  • ಮಾ ಭೂತ್ → let there not be
  • ಕಸ್ಯಚಿತ್ → for anyone
  • ಆಶಂಕಾ → doubt

ಯತ್ ಏವ ಇಹ

That which is here

  • ಯತ್ → which
  • ಏವ → indeed
  • ಇಹ → here

ಕಾರ್ಯಕಾರಣೋಪಾಧಿ ಸಮನ್ವಿತಂ

Associated with cause-and-effect adjuncts

  • ಕಾರ್ಯ → effect
  • ಕಾರಣ → cause
  • ಉಪಾಧಿ → limiting adjunct
  • ಸಮನ್ವಿತಂ → associated with

ಸಂಸಾರಧರ್ಮವತ್ ಅವಭಾಸಮಾನಂ

Appearing as though possessed of worldly attributes

  • ಸಂಸಾರಧರ್ಮವತ್ → as if having saṃsāric qualities
  • ಅವಭಾಸಮಾನಂ → appearing

ಅವಿವೇಕಿನಾಂ

To the undiscriminating

  • ಅವಿವೇಕಿನಾಂ → of those lacking discrimination

ತತ್ ಏವ ಅಮುತ್ರ

That very same is there

  • ತತ್ ಏವ → that very same
  • ಅಮುತ್ರ → there (in reality)

ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮಸ್ಥಂ

Established in its own nature

  • ಸ್ವ → own
  • ಆತ್ಮಸ್ಥಂ → abiding in itself

ನಿತ್ಯ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನಘನ ಸ್ವಭಾವಂ

Of the nature of eternal homogeneous consciousness

  • ನಿತ್ಯ → eternal
  • ವಿಜ್ಞಾನ → consciousness
  • ಘನ → solid mass, homogeneous
  • ಸ್ವಭಾವಂ → nature

ಸರ್ವಸಂಸಾರಧರ್ಮವರ್ಜಿತಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ

Brahman free from all worldly attributes

  • ಸರ್ವ → all
  • ಸಂಸಾರಧರ್ಮ → attributes of saṃsāra
  • ವರ್ಜಿತಂ → devoid of
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ → Brahman

ಯತ್ ಚ ಅಮುತ್ರ ಅಮುಷ್ಮಿನ್ ಆತ್ಮನಿ ಸ್ಥಿತಂ

That which exists there in the Self

  • ಯತ್ → which
  • ಚ → and
  • ಅಮುತ್ರ → there
  • ಆತ್ಮನಿ → in the Self
  • ಸ್ಥಿತಂ → established

ತತ್ ಅನು ಇಹ

That very same is here

  • ತತ್ → that
  • ಅನು → likewise
  • ಇಹ → here

ಕಾರ್ಯಕರಣನಾಮರೂಪೋಪಾಧಿಂ ಅನು ವಿಭಾವ್ಯಮಾನಂ

Appearing through the adjuncts of body, senses, names, and forms

  • ಕಾರ್ಯ → body, effect
  • ಕರಣ → senses
  • ನಾಮ → name
  • ರೂಪ → form
  • ಉಪಾಧಿಂ → limiting adjunct
  • ಅನು → through
  • ವಿಭಾವ್ಯಮಾನಂ → appearing

ನ ಅನ್ಯತ್

Not different

  • ನ → not
  • ಅನ್ಯತ್ → other

ಉಪಾಧಿ ಸ್ವಭಾವ ಭೇದ ದೃಷ್ಟಿ ಲಕ್ಷಣಯಾ ಅವಿದ್ಯಯಾ

Through ignorance characterized by seeing differences due to adjuncts

  • ಉಪಾಧಿ → adjunct
  • ಸ್ವಭಾವ → nature
  • ಭೇದ → difference
  • ದೃಷ್ಟಿ → perception
  • ಲಕ್ಷಣಯಾ → characterized by
  • ಅವಿದ್ಯಯಾ → by ignorance

ಮೋಹಿತಃ ಸನ್

Being deluded

  • ಮೋಹಿತಃ → deluded
  • ಸನ್ → being

ಅನ್ಯಃ ಅಹಂ

"I am different"

  • ಅನ್ಯಃ → different
  • ಅಹಂ → I

ಮತ್ತಃ ಅನ್ಯತ್ ಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ

"Brahman is different from me"

  • ಮತ್ತಃ → from me
  • ಅನ್ಯತ್ → different
  • ಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ → Supreme Brahman

ನಾನಾ ಇವ ಭಿನ್ನಂ ಇವ ಪಶ್ಯತಿ

Sees plurality as though real

  • ನಾನಾ → many
  • ಇವ → as though
  • ಭಿನ್ನಂ → separate
  • ಪಶ್ಯತಿ → sees

ಸ ಮೃತ್ಯೋಃ ಮೃತ್ಯುಂ ಆಪ್ನೋತಿ

He goes from death to death

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಮೃತ್ಯೋಃ → from death
  • ಮೃತ್ಯುಂ → death
  • ಆಪ್ನೋತಿ → attains

ಪುನಃ ಪುನಃ ಜನನಮರಣಭಾವಂ

Repeated birth and death

  • ಪುನಃ ಪುನಃ → again and again
  • ಜನನ → birth
  • ಮರಣ → death
  • ಭಾವಂ → condition

ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ತಥಾ ನ ಪಶ್ಯೇತ್

Therefore one should not see thus

  • ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ → therefore
  • ತಥಾ → in that manner
  • ನ → not
  • ಪಶ್ಯೇತ್ → should see

ವಿಜ್ಞಾನೈಕರಸಂ

Of the nature of pure undivided consciousness

  • ವಿಜ್ಞಾನ → consciousness
  • ಏಕರಸಂ → homogeneous

ನೈರಂತರ್ಯೇಣ

Without interruption

  • ನೈರಂತರ್ಯೇಣ → continuously

ಆಕಾಶವತ್ ಪರಿಪೂರ್ಣಂ

All-pervading like space

  • ಆಕಾಶವತ್ → like space
  • ಪರಿಪೂರ್ಣಂ → completely full, all-pervading

ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಏವ ಅಹಂ ಅಸ್ಮಿ

"I am Brahman alone"

  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ → Brahman
  • ಏವ → alone
  • ಅಹಂ → I
  • ಅಸ್ಮಿ → am

ಇತಿ ಪಶ್ಯೇತ್

Thus should one realize

  • ಇತಿ → thus
  • ಪಶ್ಯೇತ್ → should see, realize

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text: ಯ ಇಮಂ ಮಧ್ವದಂ ವೇದ ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ ಜೀವಮಂತಿಕಾತ್ । ಈಶಾನಂ ಭೂತಭವ್ಯಸ್ಯ ನ ತತೋ ವಿಜುಗುಪ್ಸತೇ । ಏತದ್ವೈ ತತ್ ॥ ೫ ॥   He who knows this Self as the enjoyer of the fruits of actions, as the living principle dwelling near (in the body), and as the Lord of the past and the future, does not seek to protect himself from anything thereafter. Verily, this is That.

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ಯಃ ಇಮಂ ವೇದ

Who knows this

  • ಯಃ → who
  • ಇಮಂ → this
  • ವೇದ → knows

ಮಧ್ವದಂ

The enjoyer of the fruits of actions

  • ಮಧು → sweetness, pleasant result
  • ಅದಂ → eater, enjoyer
  • ಮಧ್ವದಂ → enjoyer of the fruits (of karma)

ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ

As the Self

  • ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ → the Self

ಜೀವಂ ಅಂತಿಕಾತ್

As the living principle dwelling near

  • ಜೀವಂ → the living being, life-principle
  • ಅಂತಿಕಾತ್ → near, dwelling within the body

ಈಶಾನಂ ಭೂತಭವ್ಯಸ್ಯ

The Lord of the past and the future

  • ಈಶಾನಂ → ruler, lord
  • ಭೂತಸ್ಯ → of the past
  • ಭವ್ಯಸ್ಯ → of the future

ನ ತತಃ ವಿಜುಗುಪ್ಸತೇ

Thereafter he does not seek protection

  • ನ → not
  • ತತಃ → thereafter
  • ವಿಜುಗುಪ್ಸತೇ → seeks to protect himself, shrinks away in fear

ಏತತ್ ವೈ ತತ್

Verily, this is That

  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ವೈ → indeed
  • ತತ್ → That (Brahman taught earlier)

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text: ಕಿಂಚ, ಯಃ ಕಶ್ಚಿತ್ ಇಮಂ ಮಧ್ವದಂ ಕರ್ಮಫಲಭುಜಂ ಜೀವಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಾದಿಕಲಾಪಸ್ಯ ಧಾರಯಿತಾರಮಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ವೇದ ವಿಜಾನಾತಿ ಅಂತಿಕಾತ್ ಅಂತಿಕೇ ಸಮೀಪೇ ಈಶಾನಮ್ ಈಶಿತಾರಂ ಭೂತಭವ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಕಾಲತ್ರಯಸ್ಯ, ತತಃ ತದ್ವಿಜ್ಞಾನಾದೂರ್ಧ್ವಮಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ನ ವಿಜುಗುಪ್ಸತೇ ನ ಗೋಪಾಯಿತುಮಿಚ್ಛತಿ, ಅಭಯಪ್ರಾಪ್ತತ್ವಾತ್ । ಯಾವದ್ಧಿ ಭಯಮಧ್ಯಸ್ಥೋಽನಿತ್ಯಮಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಮನ್ಯತೇ ತಾವದ್ಗೋಪಾಯಿತುಮಿಚ್ಛತ್ಯಾತ್ಮಾನಮ್ । ಯದಾ ತು ನಿತ್ಯಮದ್ವೈತಮಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ವಿಜಾನಾತಿ, ತದಾ ಕಃ ಕಿಂ ಕುತೋ ವಾ ಗೋಪಾಯಿತುಮಿಚ್ಛೇತ್ । ಏತದ್ವೈ ತದಿತಿ ಪೂರ್ವವತ್ ॥   Further, whoever knows this Self as the enjoyer of the fruits of actions, as the living principle, as the sustainer of the aggregate of prāṇas and senses, as dwelling nearby in the body, and as the ruler of the past, present, and future — after gaining this knowledge, such a person no longer seeks to protect himself, for he has attained fearlessness.  So long as a person remains subject to fear and regards the Self as impermanent, he seeks to protect himself. But when he realizes the Self as eternal and non-dual, then who would protect whom, from what, and for what reason?  “Verily, this is That” — as explained before.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ಕಿಂಚ

Further

  • ಕಿಂಚ → moreover, further

ಯಃ ಕಶ್ಚಿತ್ ಇಮಂ ಮಧ್ವದಂ

Whoever knows this enjoyer of the fruits of action

  • ಯಃ ಕಶ್ಚಿತ್ → whoever
  • ಇಮಂ → this
  • ಮಧ್ವದಂ → enjoyer of the fruits of karma

ಕರ್ಮಫಲಭುಜಂ ಜೀವಂ

The jīva who experiences the fruits of actions

  • ಕರ್ಮ → action
  • ಫಲ → fruit, result
  • ಭುಜಂ → enjoyer
  • ಜೀವಂ → living being

ಪ್ರಾಣಾದಿಕಲಾಪಸ್ಯ ಧಾರಯಿತಾರಂ

The sustainer of the aggregate of prāṇas and senses

  • ಪ್ರಾಣಾದಿ → prāṇa and the rest
  • ಕಲಾಪಸ್ಯ → aggregate, collection
  • ಧಾರಯಿತಾರಂ → supporter, sustainer

ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ ವೇದ ವಿಜಾನಾತಿ

Knows and realizes as the Self

  • ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ → the Self
  • ವೇದ → knows
  • ವಿಜಾನಾತಿ → realizes

ಅಂತಿಕಾತ್ ಅಂತಿಕೇ ಸಮೀಪೇ

As dwelling nearby, within the body

  • ಅಂತಿಕಾತ್ → near
  • ಅಂತಿಕೇ → in proximity
  • ಸಮೀಪೇ → nearby

ಈಶಾನಂ ಈಶಿತಾರಂ

As the ruler and controller

  • ಈಶಾನಂ → ruler
  • ಈಶಿತಾರಂ → controller

ಭೂತಭವ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಕಾಲತ್ರಯಸ್ಯ

Of the three divisions of time

  • ಭೂತ → past
  • ಭವ್ಯ → future
  • ಕಾಲತ್ರಯಸ್ಯ → of the threefold time (past, present, future)

ತತಃ ತದ್ವಿಜ್ಞಾನಾತ್ ಊರ್ಧ್ವಂ

After realizing That

  • ತತಃ → thereafter
  • ತತ್-ವಿಜ್ಞಾನಾತ್ → from the knowledge of That
  • ಊರ್ಧ್ವಂ → afterwards

ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ ನ ವಿಜುಗುಪ್ಸತೇ

He does not seek to protect himself

  • ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ → himself
  • ನ → not
  • ವಿಜುಗುಪ್ಸತೇ → seeks to protect, guard

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text: ಯಃ ಪೂರ್ವಂ ತಪಸೋ ಜಾತಮದ್ಭ್ಯಃ ಪೂರ್ವಮಜಾಯತ । ಗುಹಾಂ ಪ್ರವಿಶ್ಯ ತಿಷ್ಠಂತಂ ಯೋ ಭೂತೇಭಿರ್ವ್ಯಪಶ್ಯತ । ಏತದ್ವೈ ತತ್ ॥ ೬ ॥   He who sees That which was born from tapas in the beginning, which came into being before the waters, and which, having entered the cave of the heart, abides there together with the elements—he indeed realizes That. docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text: ಯಃ ಪ್ರತ್ಯಗಾತ್ಮೇಶ್ವರಭಾವೇನ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟಃ, ಸ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮೇತ್ಯೇತದ್ದರ್ಶಯತಿ — ಯಃ ಕಶ್ಚಿನ್ಮುಮುಕ್ಷುಃ ಪೂರ್ವಂ ಪ್ರಥಮಂ ತಪಸಃ ಜ್ಞಾನಾದಿಲಕ್ಷಣಾದ್ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣ ಇತ್ಯೇತತ್ ; ಜಾತಮ್ ಉತ್ಪನ್ನಂ ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭಮ್ । ಕಿಮಪೇಕ್ಷ್ಯ ಪೂರ್ವಮಿತಿ, ಆಹ — ಅದ್ಭ್ಯಃ ಪೂರ್ವಮ್ ಅಪ್ಸಹಿತೇಭ್ಯಃ ಪಂಚಭೂತೇಭ್ಯಃ, ನ ಕೇವಲಾಭ್ಯೋಽದ್ಭ್ಯ ಇತ್ಯಭಿಪ್ರಾಯಃ । ಅಜಾಯತ ಉತ್ಪನ್ನಃ ಯಸ್ತಂ ಪ್ರಥಮಜಂ ದೇವಾದಿಶರೀರಾಣ್ಯುತ್ಪಾದ್ಯ ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಿಗುಹಾಂ ಹೃದಯಾಕಾಶಂ ಪ್ರವಿಶ್ಯ ತಿಷ್ಠಂತಂ ಶಬ್ದಾದೀನುಪಲಭಮಾನಂ ಭೂತೇಭಿಃ ಭೂತೈಃ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರಣಲಕ್ಷಣೈಃ ಸಹ ತಿಷ್ಠಂತಂ ಯೋ ವ್ಯಪಶ್ಯತ ಯಃ ಪಶ್ಯತೀತ್ಯೇತತ್ ; ಯ ಏವಂ ಪಶ್ಯತಿ, ಸ ಏತದೇವ ಪಶ್ಯತಿ — ಯತ್ತತ್ಪ್ರಕೃತಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ॥   The Self that was previously described as the inner ruler (Pratyagātman and Īśvara) is now shown to be the Self of all.  Whoever is a seeker of liberation and realizes Hiraṇyagarbha, the first-born, who arose from Brahman characterized by tapas, knowledge, and the like, and who was born before the waters—that is, before the five elements beginning with water—such a person truly sees.  Having first produced the bodies of the gods and other beings, that Hiraṇyagarbha entered the heart-space, the cave of all living beings, and remains there, experiencing sound and other sense objects, together with the body, senses, and mind.  Whoever sees Him in this manner truly sees. Such a person sees none other than the Brahman that is the subject under discussion in this section.

docs.text: ಯಾ ಪ್ರಾಣೇನ ಸಂಭವತಿ ಅದಿತಿರ್ದೇವತಾಮಯೀ । ಗುಹಾಂ ಪ್ರವಿಶ್ಯ ತಿಷ್ಠಂತೀಂ ಯಾ ಭೂತೇಭಿರ್ವ್ಯಜಾಯತ । ಏತದ್ವೈ ತತ್ ॥ ೭ ॥   That Aditi, who is constituted of all the deities, who manifests along with Prāṇa, who enters and abides in the cave of the heart, and who appears through the elements—he who realizes Her thus, realizes That. docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text: ಕಿಂಚ, ಯಾ ಸರ್ವದೇವತಾಮಯೀ ಸರ್ವದೇವತಾತ್ಮಿಕಾ ಪ್ರಾಣೇನ ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭರೂಪೇಣ ಪರಸ್ಮಾದ್ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಃ ಸಂಭವತಿ ಶಬ್ದಾದೀನಾಮದನಾತ್ ಅದಿತಿಃ ತಾಂ ಪೂರ್ವವದ್ಗುಹಾಂ ಪ್ರವಿಶ್ಯ ತಿಷ್ಠಂತೀಮ್ ಅದಿತಿಮ್ । ತಾಮೇವ ವಿಶಿನಷ್ಟಿ — ಯಾ ಭೂತೇಭಿಃ ಭೂತೈಃ ಸಮನ್ವಿತಾ ವ್ಯಜಾಯತ ಉತ್ಪನ್ನೇತ್ಯೇತತ್ ॥   Further, that Aditi, who is of the nature of all the deities and constituted by all the deities, manifests from the Supreme Brahman in the form of Hiraṇyagarbha associated with Prāṇa. She is called Aditi because she consumes (or receives) sound and the other sense objects.  That very Aditi, having entered the cave of the heart as explained before, abides there.  The mantra further specifies her nature: she is the one who manifested together with the elements; that is, she came into existence associated with the elements.

docs.text: ಅರಣ್ಯೋರ್ನಿರ್ಹಿತೋ ಜಾತವೇದಾ ಗರ್ಭ ಇವ ಸುಭೃತೋ ಗರ್ಭಿಣೀಭಿಃ । ದಿವೇ ದಿವ ಈಡ್ಯೋ ಜಾಗೃವದ್ಭಿರ್ಹವಿಷ್ಮದ್ಭಿರ್ಮನುಷ್ಯೇಭಿರಗ್ನಿಃ । ಏತದ್ವೈ ತತ್ ॥ ೮ ॥   Agni, the all-knowing fire, lies hidden in the two araṇi sticks, carefully preserved like an embryo by pregnant women. Day after day, he is worshipped by vigilant men who offer oblations. Verily, this is That.

docs.text: ಕಿಂಚ, ಯಃ ಅಧಿಯಜ್ಞಮ್ ಉತ್ತರಾಧರಾರಣ್ಯೋರ್ನಿಹಿತಃ ಸ್ಥಿತಃ ಜಾತವೇದಾ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ಪುನಃ ಸರ್ವಹವಿಷಾಂ ಭೋಕ್ತಾ ಅಧ್ಯಾತ್ಮಂ ಚ ಯೋಗಿಭಿಃ, ಗರ್ಭ ಇವ ಗರ್ಭಿಣೀಭಿಃ ಅಂತರ್ವತ್ನೀಭಿರಗರ್ಹಿತಾನ್ನಭೋಜನಾದಿನಾ ಯಥಾ ಗರ್ಭಃ ಸುಭೃತಃ ಸುಷ್ಠು ಸಮ್ಯಗ್ಭೃತೋ ಲೋಕೇ, ಇತ್ಥಮೇವ ಋತ್ವಿಗ್ಭಿರ್ಯೋಗಿಭಿಶ್ಚ ಸುಭೃತ ಇತ್ಯೇತತ್ । ಕಿಂಚ, ದಿವೇ ದಿವೇ ಅಹನ್ಯಹನಿ ಈಡ್ಯಃ ಸ್ತುತ್ಯೋ ವಂದ್ಯಶ್ಚ ಕರ್ಮಿಭಿರ್ಯೋಗಿಭಿಶ್ಚಾಧ್ವರೇ ಹೃದಯೇ ಚ ಜಾಗೃವದ್ಭಿಃ ಜಾಗರಣಶೀಲೈಃ ಅಪ್ರಮತ್ತೈರಿತ್ಯೇತತ್ । ಹವಿಷ್ಮದ್ಭಿಃ ಆಜ್ಯಾದಿಮದ್ಭಿಃ ಧ್ಯಾನಭಾವನಾವದ್ಭಿಶ್ಚ ಮನುಷ್ಯೇಭಿಃ ಮನುಷ್ಯೈಃ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ; ಏತದ್ವೈ ತತ್ ತದೇವ ಪ್ರಕೃತಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ॥   Further, that Agni, known as Jātavedas, who in the sacrificial context is hidden and established in the upper and lower araṇi sticks, and who is the enjoyer of all sacrificial offerings, is also realized inwardly by yogins.  Just as an embryo is carefully nourished and protected by pregnant women through proper food and conduct, so too this Agni is carefully sustained by priests through ritual and by yogins through contemplation.  Moreover, day after day he is worthy of praise and worship by ritualists in the sacrifice and by yogins in the heart. He is worshipped by vigilant and attentive persons who are free from negligence.  He is served by people possessing offerings such as ghee and other sacrificial materials, and also by those endowed with meditation and contemplation.  Verily, this Agni is that very Brahman which is the subject under discussion.

docs.text: ಯತಶ್ಚೋದೇತಿ ಸೂರ್ಯಃ ಅಸ್ತಂ ಯತ್ರ ಚ ಗಚ್ಛತಿ । ತಂ ದೇವಾಃ ಸರ್ವೇ ಅರ್ಪಿತಾಸ್ತದು ನಾತ್ಯೇತಿ ಕಶ್ಚನ । ಏತದ್ವೈ ತತ್ ॥ ೯ ॥   From whom the Sun rises, and into whom it sets; upon whom all the deities depend; whom none can ever transcend—verily, this is That.

docs.text: ಕಿಂಚ, ಯತಶ್ಚ ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ಪ್ರಾಣಾತ್ ಉದೇತಿ ಉತ್ತಿಷ್ಠತಿ ಸೂರ್ಯಃ, ಅಸ್ತಂ ನಿಮ್ಲೋಚನಂ ತಿರೋಧಾನಂ ಯತ್ರ ಯಸ್ಮಿನ್ನೇವ ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣೇ ಅಹನ್ಯಹನಿ ಗಚ್ಛತಿ, ತಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಮಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ದೇವಾಃ ಸರ್ವೇ ಅಗ್ನ್ಯಾದಯಃ ಅಧಿದೈವಂ ವಾಗಾದಯಶ್ಚಾಧ್ಯಾತ್ಮಂ ಸರ್ವೇ ವಿಶ್ವೇ ಅರಾ ಇವ ರಥನಾಭೌ ಅರ್ಪಿತಾಃ ಸಂಪ್ರವೇಶಿತಾಃ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಕಾಲೇ । ಸೋಽಪಿ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮೈವ । ತತ್ ಏತತ್ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಕಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ, ತದು ನಾತ್ಯೇತಿ ನಾತೀತ್ಯ ತದಾತ್ಮಕತಾಂ ತದನ್ಯತ್ವಂ ಗಚ್ಛತಿ, ಕಶ್ಚನ ಕಶ್ಚಿದಪಿ ಏತದ್ವೈ ತತ್ ॥   Further, from that Prāṇa the Sun rises and becomes manifest; and into that very Prāṇa it sets and disappears day after day.  Upon that Prāṇa, which is the Self, all the deities such as Agni in the cosmic sphere, and speech and the other faculties in the individual sphere, are established. They are fixed in it just as the spokes of a wheel are fixed in the hub.  That Prāṇa is itself Brahman.  This Brahman is the Self of all. No one can go beyond It. No one can transcend Its nature and become something other than It, for there exists nothing apart from It.  Verily, this is That.

  • ಹಿ → indeed
  • ಅಕಾಮಾಃ → free from desires

ತೇ ಶುಕ್ರಮ್ ಏತತ್ ಅತಿವರ್ತಂತಿ ಧೀರಾಃ

Those wise ones transcend this seed/source of birth.

  • ತೇ → they
  • ಶುಕ್ರಮ್ → seed, source of generation
  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ಅತಿವರ್ತಂತಿ → transcend
  • ಧೀರಾಃ → wise ones

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text:
ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಸ ವೇದ ಜಾನಾತಿ ಏತತ್ ಯಥೋಕ್ತಲಕ್ಷಣಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಪರಮಂ ಪ್ರಕೃಷ್ಟಂ ಧಾಮ ಸರ್ವಕಾಮಾನಾಮಾಶ್ರಯಮಾಸ್ಪದಮ್, ಯತ್ರ ಯಸ್ಮಿನ್ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಿ ಧಾಮ್ನಿ ವಿಶ್ವಂ ಸಮಸ್ತಂ ಜಗತ್ ನಿಹಿತಮ್ ಅರ್ಪಿತಮ್, ಯಚ್ಚ ಸ್ವೇನ ಜ್ಯೋತಿಷಾ ಭಾತಿ ಶುಭ್ರಂ ಶುದ್ಧಮ್, ತಮಪ್ಯೇವಂವಿಧಮಾತ್ಮಜ್ಞಂ ಪುರುಷಂ ಯೇ ಹಿ ಅಕಾಮಾಃ ವಿಭೂತಿತೃಷ್ಣಾವರ್ಜಿತಾ ಮುಮುಕ್ಷವಃ ಸಂತಃ ಉಪಾಸತೇ ಪರಮಿವ ದೇವಮ್, ತೇ ಶುಕ್ರಂ ನೃಬೀಜಂ ಯದೇತತ್ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧಂ ಶರೀರೋಪಾದಾನಕಾರಣಮ್ ಅತಿವರ್ತಂತಿ ಅತಿಗಚ್ಛಂತಿ ಧೀರಾಃ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮಂತಃ, ನ ಪುನರ್ಯೋನಿಂ ಪ್ರಸರ್ಪಂತಿ । ‘ನ ಪುನಃ ಕ್ವ ರತಿಂ ಕರೋತಿ’ ಇತಿ ಶ್ರುತೇಃ । ಅತಸ್ತಂ ಪೂಜಯೇದಿತ್ಯಭಿಪ್ರಾಯಃ ॥ Because he knows this Brahman characterized as previously described—the supreme Reality, the support and abode of all desires, in which the entire universe is established and offered, and which shines by its own light as pure—that knower of the Self, being of such nature, is meditated upon by seekers of liberation who are free from craving for powers and enjoyments, as though He were the Supreme Lord Himself. Those wise ones transcend this seed of human birth, namely the well-known cause of embodiment. They do not again enter the womb. As the scripture says: > "He does not again delight in birth." Therefore, the intention is that such a knower should indeed be worshipped.

ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಸಃ ವೇದ ಜಾನಾತಿ ಏತತ್ ಯಥೋಕ್ತಲಕ್ಷಣಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ

Because he knows this Brahman characterized as previously described.

  • ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ → because
  • ಸಃ → he
  • ವೇದ → knows
  • ಜಾನಾತಿ → understands
  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ಯಥೋಕ್ತಲಕ್ಷಣಂ → having the characteristics already described
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ → Brahman

ಪರಮಂ ಪ್ರಕೃಷ್ಟಂ ಧಾಮ ಸರ್ವಕಾಮಾನಾಂ ಆಶ್ರಯಂ ಆಸ್ಪದಂ

The supreme abode and support of all desires.

  • ಪರಮಂ → supreme
  • ಪ್ರಕೃಷ್ಟಂ → highest
  • ಧಾಮ → abode
  • ಸರ್ವಕಾಮಾನಾಂ → of all desires
  • ಆಶ್ರಯಂ → support
  • ಆಸ್ಪದಂ → resting place

ಯತ್ರ ಯಸ್ಮಿನ್ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಿ ಧಾಮ್ನಿ ವಿಶ್ವಂ ಸಮಸ್ತಂ ಜಗತ್ ನಿಹಿತಂ ಅರ್ಪಿತಂ

In which Brahman the entire universe is established and offered.

  • ಯತ್ರ → wherein
  • ಯಸ್ಮಿನ್ → in which
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಿ → in Brahman
  • ಧಾಮ್ನಿ → in the luminous abode
  • ವಿಶ್ವಂ → universe
  • ಸಮಸ್ತಂ → entire
  • ಜಗತ್ → world
  • ನಿಹಿತಂ → placed
  • ಅರ್ಪಿತಂ → offered/resting

ಯತ್ ಚ ಸ್ವೇನ ಜ್ಯೋತಿಷಾ ಭಾತಿ ಶುಭ್ರಂ ಶುದ್ಧಂ

And which shines by its own light as pure.

  • ಯತ್ → which
  • ಚ → and
  • ಸ್ವೇನ → by its own
  • ಜ್ಯೋತಿಷಾ → light
  • ಭಾತಿ → shines
  • ಶುಭ್ರಂ → luminous/pure
  • ಶುದ್ಧಂ → pure

ತಂ ಅಪಿ ಏವಂವಿಧಂ ಆತ್ಮಜ್ಞಂ ಪುರುಷಂ ಯೇ ಹಿ ಅಕಾಮಾಃ ವಿಭೂತಿತೃಷ್ಣಾ ವರ್ಜಿತಾಃ ಮುಮುಕ್ಷವಃ ಸಂತಃ ಉಪಾಸತೇ

That knower of the Self is meditated upon by desireless seekers of liberation free from craving for powers.

  • ತಂ → that
  • ಅಪಿ → indeed
  • ಏವಂವಿಧಂ → of such nature
  • ಆತ್ಮಜ್ಞಂ → knower of Self
  • ಪುರುಷಂ → person
  • ಯೇ → who
  • ಹಿ → indeed
  • ಅಕಾಮಾಃ → desireless
  • ವಿಭೂತಿ → powers/glories
  • ತೃಷ್ಣಾ → craving
  • ವರ್ಜಿತಾಃ → free from
  • ಮುಮುಕ್ಷವಃ → seekers of liberation
  • ಸಂತಃ → being
  • ಉಪಾಸತೇ → meditate upon/worship

ಪರಂ ಇವ ದೇವಂ

As though He were the Supreme Lord.

  • ಪರಂ → supreme
  • ಇವ → as though
  • ದೇವಂ → divine Lord

ತೇ ಶುಕ್ರಂ ನೃಬೀಜಂ ಯತ್ ಏತತ್ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧಂ ಶರೀರೋಪಾದಾನಕಾರಣಂ ಅತಿವರ್ತಂತಿ ಅತಿಗಚ್ಛಂತಿ ಧೀರಾಃ

Those wise ones transcend the seed of human birth, the cause of embodiment.

  • ತೇ → they
  • ಶುಕ್ರಂ → seed
  • ನೃಬೀಜಂ → human seed
  • ಯತ್ → which
  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧಂ → well-known
  • ಶರೀರೋಪಾದಾನಕಾರಣಂ → cause of bodily embodiment
  • ಅತಿವರ್ತಂತಿ → transcend
  • ಅತಿಗಚ್ಛಂತಿ → go beyond
  • ಧೀರಾಃ → wise ones

ನ ಪುನಃ ಯೋನಿಂ ಪ್ರಸರ್ಪಂತಿ

They do not again enter the womb.

  • ನ → not
  • ಪುನಃ → again
  • ಯೋನಿಂ → womb/birth
  • ಪ್ರಸರ್ಪಂತಿ → enter/proceed into

ನ ಪುನಃ ಕ್ವ ರತಿಂ ಕರೋತಿ ಇತಿ ಶ್ರುತೇಃ

As scripture says: “He does not again delight in birth.”

  • ನ → not
  • ಪುನಃ → again
  • ಕ್ವ → anywhere
  • ರತಿಂ → attachment/delight/like
  • ಕರೋತಿ → makes
  • ಇತಿ → thus
  • ಶ್ರುತೇಃ → from scripture

ಅತಃ ತಂ ಪೂಜಯೇತ್ ಇತಿ ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯಃ

Therefore the intention is that such a knower should be worshipped.

  • ಅತಃ → therefore
  • ತಂ → him
  • ಪೂಜಯೇತ್ → should worship
  • ಇತಿ → thus
  • ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯಃ → intention

docs.title: ಅವತಾರಿಕಾಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text:
ಮಂತ್ರೋಕ್ತಸ್ಯಾರ್ಥಸ್ಯ ವಿಸ್ತರಾನುವಾದೀದಂ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಮಾರಭ್ಯತೇ । ಋಷಿಪ್ರಶ್ನಪ್ರತಿವಾಚನಾಖ್ಯಾಯಿಕಾ ತು ವಿದ್ಯಾಸ್ತುತಯೇ । ಏವಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಸಂವಾಸಾದಿತಪೋಯುಕ್ತೈರ್ಗ್ರಾಹ್ಯಾ, ಪಿಪ್ಪಲಾದವತ್ಸರ್ವಜ್ಞಕಲ್ಪೈರಾಚಾರ್ಯೈಃ ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಾ ಚ, ನ ಯೇನ ಕೇನಚಿದಿತಿ ವಿದ್ಯಾಂ ಸ್ತೌತಿ । ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಾದಿಸಾಧನಸೂಚನಾಚ್ಚ ತತ್ಕರ್ತವ್ಯತಾ ಸ್ಯಾತ್ — This Brāhmaṇa section is now commenced as a detailed exposition of the meaning that was briefly stated in the mantra. The narrative in the form of the sages asking questions and receiving answers is intended for the glorification of this knowledge (Brahma-vidyā). The purpose is to praise the knowledge by showing that it is fit to be received only by those who have undergone austerities such as living in brahmacarya for a year, residing with the teacher, and observing other disciplines. Likewise, it is to be taught only by teachers who, like Pippalāda, are comparable to omniscient persons; it is not something that may be taught by just anyone. Thus the Upaniṣad extols the greatness of this knowledge. Furthermore, by indicating disciplines such as brahmacarya and the like, the text also establishes that these are duties to be undertaken by seekers of knowledge.

ಮಂತ್ರೋಕ್ತಸ್ಯಾರ್ಥಸ್ಯ ವಿಸ್ತರಾನುವಾದೀ ಇದಂ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಮಾರಭ್ಯತೇ

This Brāhmaṇa portion is begun as a detailed explanation of the meaning expressed in the mantra.

  • ಮಂತ್ರೋಕ್ತಸ್ಯ → stated in the mantra
  • ಅರ್ಥಸ್ಯ → of the meaning
  • ವಿಸ್ತರ → detailed
  • ಅನುವಾದೀ → explanatory restatement
  • ಇದಂ → this
  • ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಂ → Brāhmaṇa section
  • ಆರಭ್ಯತೇ → is commenced

(Mundaka is mantra and Prasna is brahmana )

ಋಷಿಪ್ರಶ್ನಪ್ರತಿವಾಚನಾಖ್ಯಾಯಿಕಾ ತು ವಿದ್ಯಾಸ್ತುತಯೇ

The narrative consisting of the sages' questions and answers is for the praise of the knowledge.

  • ಋಷಿ → sage
  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನ → question
  • ಪ್ರತಿವಾಚನ → answer
  • ಆಖ್ಯಾಯಿಕಾ → narrative account
  • ತು → indeed
  • ವಿದ್ಯಾ → knowledge
  • ಸ್ತುತಯೇ → for praise

ಏವಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಸಂವಾಸಾದಿತಪೋಯುಕ್ತೈರ್ಗ್ರಾಹ್ಯಾ

Thus this knowledge is to be received by those endowed with austerities such as living for a year in brahmacarya and residing with the teacher.

  • ಏವಂ → thus
  • ಸಂವತ್ಸರ → one year
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯ → celibate discipline
  • ಸಂವಾಸ → residence with the teacher (gurukula)
  • ಆದಿ → and other
  • ತಪಃ → austerities
  • ಯುಕ್ತೈಃ → endowed with
  • ಗ್ರಾಹ್ಯಾ → fit to be received

ಪಿಪ್ಪಲಾದವತ್ಸರ್ವಜ್ಞಕಲ್ಪೈರಾಚಾರ್ಯೈಃ ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಾ ಚ

And it is to be taught by teachers who, like Pippalāda, are comparable to omniscient persons.

  • ಪಿಪ್ಪಲಾದವತ್ → like Pippalāda
  • ಸರ್ವಜ್ಞಕಲ್ಪೈಃ → comparable to omniscient beings (kalpa = like)
  • ಆಚಾರ್ಯೈಃ → by teachers
  • ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಾ → should be taught
  • ಚ → and

ನ ಯೇನ ಕೇನಚಿದಿತಿ ವಿದ್ಯಾಂ ಸ್ತೌತಿ

By implying that it should not be taught by just anyone, the text praises the knowledge.

  • ನ → not
  • ಯೇನ ಕೇನಚಿತ್ → by any random person
  • ಇತಿ → thus
  • ವಿದ್ಯಾಂ → the knowledge
  • ಸ್ತೌತಿ → praises

ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಾದಿಸಾಧನಸೂಚನಾಚ್ಚ ತತ್ಕರ್ತವ್ಯತಾ ಸ್ಯಾತ್

And by indicating disciplines such as brahmacarya, it establishes that these are to be practiced.

  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಾದಿ → brahmacarya and similar disciplines
  • ಸಾಧನ → means/spiritual disciplines
  • ಸೂಚನಾತ್ → by indicating
  • ಚ → and
  • ತತ್ → those
  • ಕರ್ತವ್ಯತಾ → obligatoriness, duty
  • ಸ್ಯಾತ್ → is established

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text:
ಸುಕೇಶಾ ಚ ಭಾರದ್ವಾಜಃ ಶೈಬ್ಯಶ್ಚ ಸತ್ಯಕಾಮಃ ಸೌರ್ಯಾಯಣೀ ಚ ಗಾರ್ಗ್ಯಃ ಕೌಸಲ್ಯಶ್ಚಾಶ್ವಲಾಯನೋ ಭಾರ್ಗವೋ ವೈದರ್ಭಿಃ ಕಬಂಧೀ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಸ್ತೇ ಹೈತೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪರಾ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನಿಷ್ಠಾಃ ಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಾನ್ವೇಷಮಾಣಾ ಏಷ ಹ ವೈ ತತ್ಸರ್ವಂ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯತೀತಿ ತೇ ಹ ಸಮಿತ್ಪಾಣಯೋ ಭಗವಂತಂ ಪಿಪ್ಪಲಾದಮುಪಸನ್ನಾಃ ॥ ೧ ॥ Sukeśa, the son of Bharadvāja; Satyakāma, the son of Śibi; Gārgya of the lineage of Sūryāyaṇa; Kauśalya, the son of Aśvala; Bhārgava of Vidarbha; and Kabandhi, the son of Kātyāyana—these seekers were devoted to Brahman, established in Brahman, and desirous of knowing the Supreme Brahman. Thinking, “Surely this revered teacher will explain all this to us,” they approached the venerable Pippalāda, carrying sacrificial fuel in their hands.

ಸುಕೇಶಾ ಚ ಭಾರದ್ವಾಜಃ

And Sukeśa, the son of Bharadvāja.

  • ಸುಕೇಶಃ → Sukeśa
  • ಚ → and
  • ಭಾರದ್ವಾಜಃ → descendant/son of Bharadvāja

ಶೈಬ್ಯಃ ಚ ಸತ್ಯಕಾಮಃ

And Satyakāma, the descendant of Śibi.

  • ಶೈಬ್ಯಃ → descendant of Śibi
  • ಸತ್ಯಕಾಮಃ → Satyakāma

ಸೌರ್ಯಾಯಣೀ ಚ ಗಾರ್ಗ್ಯಃ

And Gārgya of the Sūryāyaṇa lineage.

  • ಸೌರ್ಯಾಯಣೀ → belonging to Sūryāyaṇa lineage
  • ಗಾರ್ಗ್ಯಃ → Gārgya

ಕೌಸಲ್ಯಃ ಚ ಆಶ್ವಲಾಯನಃ

And Kauśalya, son of Aśvala.

  • ಕೌಸಲ್ಯಃ → Kauśalya
  • ಆಶ್ವಲಾಯನಃ → descendant of Aśvala

ಭಾರ್ಗವಃ ವೈದರ್ಭಿಃ

Bhārgava of Vidarbha.

  • ಭಾರ್ಗವಃ → descendant of Bhṛgu
  • ವೈದರ್ಭಿಃ → from Vidarbha

ಕಬಂಧೀ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ

Kabandhi, son of Kātyāyana.

  • ಕಬಂಧೀ → Kabandhi
  • ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ → descendant of Kātyāyana

ತೇ ಹ ಏತೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪರಾಃ

These indeed were devoted to Brahman.

  • ತೇ → they
  • ಹ → indeed
  • ಏತೇ → these
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪರಾಃ → having Brahman as their supreme goal

ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನಿಷ್ಠಾಃ

Established in Brahman.

  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನಿಷ್ಠಾಃ → steadfast in contemplation of Brahman

In this context, Śaṅkara generally takes this as being devoted to scriptural pursuit and contemplation leading toward Brahma-jñāna.

ಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಅನ್ವೇಷಮಾಣಾಃ

Seeking the Supreme Brahman.

  • ಪರಂ → supreme
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ → Brahman
  • ಅನ್ವೇಷಮಾಣಾಃ → searching for, seeking

ಏಷಃ ಹ ವೈ ತತ್ ಸರ್ವಂ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯತಿ ಇತಿ

Thinking, “Surely he will explain all that.”

  • ಏಷಃ → this teacher
  • ಹ ವೈ → indeed
  • ತತ್ ಸರ್ವಂ → all that (Brahman-related knowledge)
  • ವಕ್ಷ್ಯತಿ → will explain
  • ಇತಿ → thus

ತೇ ಹ ಸಮಿತ್ಪಾಣಯಃ

They approached carrying sacrificial fuel in their hands.

  • ತೇ → they
  • ಹ → indeed

Samit-pāṇi is symbolic: humility readiness for discipleship willingness to serve the teacher

ಭಗವಂತಂ ಪಿಪ್ಪಲಾದಂ ಉಪಸನ್ನಾಃ

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text:
ಸುಕೇಶಾ ಚ ನಾಮತಃ, ಭರದ್ವಾಜಸ್ಯಾಪತ್ಯಂ ಭಾರದ್ವಾಜಃ । ಶೈಬ್ಯಶ್ಚ ಶಿಬೇರಪತ್ಯಂ ಶೈಬ್ಯಃ, ಸತ್ಯಕಾಮೋ ನಾಮತಃ । ಸೌರ್ಯಾಯಣೀ ಸೂರ್ಯಸ್ಯಾಪತ್ಯಂ ಸೌರ್ಯಃ, ತಸ್ಯಾಪತ್ಯಂ ಸೌರ್ಯಾಯಣಿಃ ; ಛಾಂದಸಂ ಸೌರ್ಯಾಯಣೀತಿ ; ಗಾರ್ಗ್ಯಃ ಗರ್ಗಗೋತ್ರೋತ್ಪನ್ನಃ । ಕೌಸಲ್ಯಶ್ಚ ನಾಮತಃ, ಅಶ್ವಲಸ್ಯಾಪತ್ಯಮಾಶ್ವಲಾಯನಃ । ಭಾರ್ಗವಃ ಭೃಗೋರ್ಗೋತ್ರಾಪತ್ಯಂ ಭಾರ್ಗವಃ, ವೈದರ್ಭಿಃ ವಿದರ್ಭೇಷು ಭವಃ । ಕಬಂಧೀ ನಾಮತಃ, ಕತ್ಯಸ್ಯಾಪತ್ಯಂ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ ; ವಿದ್ಯಮಾನಃ ಪ್ರಪಿತಾಮಹೋ ಯಸ್ಯ ಸಃ ; ಯುವಪ್ರತ್ಯಯಃ । ತೇ ಹ ಏತೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪರಾಃ ಅಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಪರತ್ವೇನ ಗತಾಃ, ತದನುಷ್ಠಾನನಿಷ್ಠಾಶ್ಚ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನಿಷ್ಠಾಃ, ಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಅನ್ವೇಷಮಾಣಾಃ ಕಿಂ ತತ್ ಯನ್ನಿತ್ಯಂ ವಿಜ್ಞೇಯಮಿತಿ ತತ್ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತ್ಯರ್ಥಂ ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ ಯತಿಷ್ಯಾಮ ಇತ್ಯೇವಂ ತದನ್ವೇಷಣಂ ಕುರ್ವಂತಃ, ತದಧಿಗಮಾಯ ಏಷ ಹ ವೈ ತತ್ಸರ್ವಂ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯತೀತಿ ಆಚಾರ್ಯಮುಪಜಗ್ಮುಃ । ಕಥಮ್ ? ತೇ ಹ ಸಮಿತ್ಪಾಣಯಃ ಸಮಿದ್ಭಾರಗೃಹೀತಹಸ್ತಾಃ ಸಂತಃ, ಭಗವಂತಂ ಪೂಜಾವಂತಂ ಪಿಪ್ಪಲಾದಮಾಚಾರ್ಯಮ್ ಉಪಸನ್ನಾಃ ಉಪಜಗ್ಮುಃ ॥ Sukeśa is the personal name; being the son of Bharadvāja, he is called Bhāradvāja. Likewise, Śaibya means a descendant of Śibi, while Satyakāma is his personal name. Sauryāyaṇi means a descendant of Sūrya; "Sauryāyaṇi" is a Vedic form of expression. Gārgya means one born in the lineage of Garga. Kauśalya is the personal name, and Āśvalāyana means a descendant of Aśvala. Bhārgava means one descended from the lineage of Bhṛgu, and Vaidarbhi means one belonging to the region of Vidarbha. Kabandhi is the personal name, and Kātyāyana means a descendant of Katya; the suffix indicates that the ancestor (Katya) is still remembered in the lineage. These indeed were devoted to Brahman, taking the lower Brahman as their supreme goal and being steadfast in its contemplation and worship; hence they are called Brahmaniṣṭhas. At the same time, they were seekers of the Supreme Brahman, wondering, "What is that eternal Reality which ought to be known?" Desiring to attain That, and resolving, "We shall strive in every way to realize It," they engaged in the search for the Supreme Brahman. Thinking, "Surely this teacher will explain all that to us," they approached him. How did they approach? Carrying bundles of sacrificial fuel in their hands, they approached the revered and venerable teacher Pippalāda.

ಸುಕೇಶಾ ಚ ನಾಮತಃ

"Sukeśa" is the personal name.

  • ಸುಕೇಶಾ → Sukeśa
  • ನಾಮತಃ → by name

  • ಶೈಬ್ಯಃ → descendant of Śibi
  • ಶಿಬೇಃ → of Śibi
  • ಅಪತ್ಯಂ → offspring

ಛಾಂದಸಂ ಸೌರ್ಯಾಯಣೀತಿ

"Sauryāyaṇi" is the Vedic (metrical) form.

  • ಛಾಂದಸಂ → Vedic usage
  • ಸೌರ್ಯಾಯಣೀತಿ → the form "Sauryāyaṇi"

  • ಗೋತ್ರ → lineage

ಅಶ್ವಲಸ್ಯ ಅಪತ್ಯಂ ಆಶ್ವಲಾಯನಃ

  • ಅಪತ್ಯಂ → offspring
  • ಆಶ್ವಲಾಯನಃ → descendant of Aśvala

ಭಾರ್ಗವಃ ಭೃಗೋಃ ಗೋತ್ರಾಪತ್ಯಂ

ಕತ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಅಪತ್ಯಂ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ

  • ಅಪತ್ಯಂ → offspring
  • ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ → descendant of Katya

ತೇ ಹ ಏತೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪರಾಃ

These indeed were devoted to Brahman.

  • ಏತೇ → these
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪರಾಃ → devoted to Brahman

ಅಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಪರತ್ವೇನ ಗತಾಃ

They had taken the lower Brahman as their immediate object of worship.

  • ಅಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ → lower Brahman (saguṇa Brahman)
  • ಪರತ್ವೇನ → as supreme

This is an important Śaṅkara gloss. Here "ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪರಾಃ" is interpreted as seekers devoted to meditation upon saguṇa Brahman.

ತದನುಷ್ಠಾನನಿಷ್ಠಾಃ ಚ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನಿಷ್ಠಾಃ

And they were steadfast in its practice.

  • ನಿಷ್ಠಾಃ → steadfast
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನಿಷ್ಠಾಃ → devoted to Brahman

ಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಅನ್ವೇಷಮಾಣಾಃ

Seeking the Supreme Brahman.

  • ಪಾಣಯಃ → in their hands

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text: ಅಥೋತ್ತರೇಣ ತಪಸಾ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ ವಿದ್ಯಯಾತ್ಮಾನಮನ್ವಿಷ್ಯಾದಿತ್ಯಮಭಿಜಯಂತೇ । ಏತದ್ವೈ ಪ್ರಾಣಾನಾಮಾಯತನಮೇತದಮೃತಮಭಯಮೇತತ್ಪರಾಯಣಮೇತಸ್ಮಾನ್ನ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಂತ ಇತ್ಯೇಷ ನಿರೋಧಃ । ತದೇಷ ಶ್ಲೋಕಃ ॥ ೧೦ ॥   But by the northern path, through austerity, brahmacarya, faith, and knowledge, seeking the Self, they attain the Sun. This indeed is the abode of all prāṇas; this is the immortal, the fearless, the supreme goal. From this they do not return again. This is the final cessation of return. Concerning this, there is the following verse.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text: ಅಥ ಉತ್ತರೇಣ ಅಯನೇನ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತೇರಂಶಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಮತ್ತಾರಮ್ ಆದಿತ್ಯಮ್ ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ । ಕೇನ ? ತಪಸಾ ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಜಯೇನ । ವಿಶೇಷತೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ ವಿದ್ಯಯಾ ಚ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯಾತ್ಮವಿಷಯಯಾ ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಸೂರ್ಯಂ ಜಗತಃ ತಸ್ಥುಷಶ್ಚ ಅನ್ವಿಷ್ಯ ಅಹಮಸ್ಮೀತಿ ವಿದಿತ್ವಾ ಆದಿತ್ಯಮ್ ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಪ್ನುವಂತಿ । ಏತದ್ವೈ ಆಯತನಂ ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಾನಾಂ ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯಮಾಯತನಮ್ ಆಶ್ರಯಃ ಏತತ್ ಅಮೃತಮ್ ಅವಿನಾಶಿ ಅಭಯಮ್ ಅತ ಏವ ಭಯವರ್ಜಿತಮ್ ನ ಚಂದ್ರವತ್ಕ್ಷಯವೃದ್ಧಿಭಯವತ್ ; ಏತತ್ ಪರಾಯಣಂ ಪರಾ ಗತಿರ್ವಿದ್ಯಾವತಾಂ ಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಚ ಜ್ಞಾನವತಾಮ್ ಏತಸ್ಮಾನ್ನ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಂತೇ ಯಥೇತರೇ ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣ ಇತಿ ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಏಷಃ ಅವಿದುಷಾಂ ನಿರೋಧಃ, ಆದಿತ್ಯಾದ್ಧಿ ನಿರುದ್ಧಾ ಅವಿದ್ವಾಂಸಃ । ನೈತೇ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಮಾದಿತ್ಯಮಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಮಭಿಪ್ರಾಪ್ನುವಂತಿ । ಸ ಹಿ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ ಕಾಲಾತ್ಮಾ ಅವಿದುಷಾಂ ನಿರೋಧಃ । ತತ್ ತತ್ರಾಸ್ಮಿನ್ನರ್ಥೇ ಏಷಃ ಶ್ಲೋಕಃ ಮಂತ್ರಃ ॥   By the northern path, they attain Āditya, who is Prāṇa, the eater, and an aspect of Prajāpati.  By what means? Through tapas, which is control of the senses; especially through brahmacarya, faith, and knowledge concerning the nature of Prajāpati. Seeking the Self in the form of Prāṇa, the Sun, which is the inner principle of both the moving and the unmoving universe, and realizing “I am that,” they attain the Sun.  This indeed is the common abode and support of all prāṇas. It is immortal, imperishable, and therefore fearless, unlike the Moon, which is subject to increase and decrease and hence associated with fear.  This is the supreme goal of those endowed with knowledge and of those whose actions are accompanied by knowledge. From this they do not return, unlike those who perform only rituals.  Therefore, this (Sun) is the limit beyond which the ignorant do not pass. The ignorant are held back by Āditya and do not attain the year, the Sun, Prāṇa, or the Self. For the year, which is of the nature of time, serves as the boundary for the ignorant.  Concerning this subject, the following Vedic verse is declared.

ಅಥ ಉತ್ತರೇಣ ಅಯನೇನ

By the northern path

  • ಅಥ → now, but
  • ಉತ್ತರೇಣ → by the northern
  • ಅಯನೇನ → path, course

ಪ್ರಜಾಪತೇಃ ಅಂಶಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಅತ್ತಾರಂ ಆದಿತ್ಯಮ್ ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ

They attain Āditya, who is Prāṇa, the eater, and an aspect of Prajāpati

  • ಪ್ರಜಾಪತೇಃ → of Prajāpati
  • ಅಂಶಂ → aspect, manifestation
  • ಪ್ರಾಣಂ → Prāṇa
  • ಅತ್ತಾರಂ → eater
  • ಆದಿತ್ಯಮ್ → the Sun

ಕೇನ

By what means?

  • ಕೇನ → by what

ತಪಸಾ ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಜಯೇನ

Through tapas, namely mastery over the senses

  • ತಪಸಾ → through austerity
  • ಇಂದ್ರಿಯ → senses
  • ಜಯೇನ → through conquest

ವಿಶೇಷತಃ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ ವಿದ್ಯಯಾ ಚ

Especially through brahmacarya, faith, and knowledge

  • ವಿಶೇಷತಃ → especially
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ → through brahmacarya
  • ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ → through faith
  • ವಿದ್ಯಯಾ → through knowledge
  • ಚ → and

ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯಾತ್ಮವಿಷಯಯಾ

Knowledge concerning the nature of Prajāpati

  • ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯ → relating to Prajāpati
  • ಆತ್ಮ → nature, self
  • ವಿಷಯಯಾ → concerning

ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಸೂರ್ಯಂ

The Self as Prāṇa and the Sun

  • ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ → the Self
  • ಪ್ರಾಣಂ → Prāṇa
  • ಸೂರ್ಯಂ → the Sun

ಜಗತಃ ತಸ್ಥುಷಃ ಚ

Of the moving and the unmoving universe

  • ಜಗತಃ → of the moving world
  • ತಸ್ಥುಷಃ → of the stationary world
  • ಚ → and

ಅನ್ವಿಷ್ಯ

Having sought

  • ಅನ್ವಿಷ್ಯ → seeking, inquiring into

ಅಹಂ ಅಸ್ಮಿ ಇತಿ ವಿದಿತ್ವಾ

Having realized “I am that”

  • ಅಹಂ → I
  • ಅಸ್ಮಿ → am
  • ಇತಿ → thus
  • ವಿದಿತ್ವಾ → having known

ಆದಿತ್ಯಮ್ ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ

They attain Āditya

  • ಆದಿತ್ಯಮ್ → the Sun
  • ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ → attain

ಏತತ್ ವೈ ಆಯತನಂ ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಾನಾಂ

This indeed is the abode of all prāṇas

  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ವೈ → indeed
  • ಆಯತನಂ → abode
  • ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಾನಾಂ → of all beings

The common support and refuge

  • ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯಂ → common, universal
  • ಆಯತನಂ → abode
  • ಆಶ್ರಯಃ → support

ಏತತ್ ಅಮೃತಮ್ ಅವಿನಾಶಿ

This is immortal and imperishable

  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ಅಮೃತಮ್ → immortal
  • ಅವಿನಾಶಿ → indestructible

ಅಭಯಮ್ ಅತ ಏವ ಭಯವರ್ಜಿತಮ್

Therefore it is fearless

  • ಅಭಯಮ್ → fearless
  • ಅತ ಏವ → therefore
  • ಭಯವರ್ಜಿತಮ್ → devoid of fear

ನ ಚಂದ್ರವತ್ ಕ್ಷಯವೃದ್ಧಿಭಯವತ್

Not like the Moon, which is subject to waxing and waning

  • ನ → not
  • ಚಂದ್ರವತ್ → like the Moon
  • ಕ್ಷಯ → decrease
  • ವೃದ್ಧಿ → increase
  • ಭಯವತ್ → associated with fear

ಏತತ್ ಪರಾಯಣಂ ಪರಾ ಗತಿಃ

This is the highest goal

  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ಪರಾಯಣಂ → supreme refuge
  • ಪರಾ → highest
  • ಗತಿಃ → destination

ವಿದ್ಯಾವತಾಂ ಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಚ ಜ್ಞಾನವತಾಮ್

For those possessed of knowledge and action accompanied by knowledge

  • ವಿದ್ಯಾವತಾಂ → of the learned
  • ಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ → of performers of action
  • ಚ → and
  • ಜ್ಞಾನವತಾಮ್ → of those possessing knowledge

ಏತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ನ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಂತೇ

From this they do not return

  • ಏತಸ್ಮಾತ್ → from this
  • ನ → not
  • ಪುನಃ → again
  • ಆವರ್ತಂತೇ → return

ಯಥಾ ಇತರೇ ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಃ

Unlike those devoted only to ritual action

  • ಯಥಾ → as
  • ಇತರೇ → others
  • ಕೇವಲ → only
  • ಕರ್ಮಿಣಃ → ritualists

ಏಷಃ ಅವಿದುಷಾಂ ನಿರೋಧಃ

This is the limit of the ignorant

  • ಏಷಃ → this
  • ಅವಿದುಷಾಂ → of the ignorant
  • ನಿರೋಧಃ → boundary, limitation

ಆದಿತ್ಯಾತ್ ಹಿ ನಿರುದ್ಧಾಃ ಅವಿದ್ವಾಂಸಃ

The ignorant are stopped at Āditya

  • ಆದಿತ್ಯಾತ್ → by Āditya
  • ಹಿ → indeed
  • ನಿರುದ್ಧಾಃ → restrained, held back
  • ಅವಿದ್ವಾಂಸಃ → ignorant persons

ನ ಏತೇ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ ಆದಿತ್ಯಂ ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಪ್ನುವಂತಿ

They do not attain the year, the Sun, Prāṇa, or the Self

  • ನ → not
  • ಏತೇ → these
  • ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ → the year
  • ಆದಿತ್ಯಂ → the Sun
  • ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ → the Self
  • ಪ್ರಾಣಂ → Prāṇa
  • ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಪ್ನುವಂತಿ → attain

ಸಃ ಹಿ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ ಕಾಲಾತ್ಮಾ

For the year is of the nature of time

  • ಸಃ → that
  • ಹಿ → indeed
  • ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ → year
  • ಕಾಲಾತ್ಮಾ → of the nature of time

ಅವಿದುಷಾಂ ನಿರೋಧಃ

The boundary for the ignorant

  • ಅವಿದುಷಾಂ → of the ignorant
  • ನಿರೋಧಃ → limit, barrier

ತತ್ ತತ್ರ ಅಸ್ಮಿನ್ ಅರ್ಥೇ

Concerning this matter

  • ತತ್ → that
  • ತತ್ರ → there
  • ಅಸ್ಮಿನ್ → this
  • ಅರ್ಥೇ → subject

ಏಷಃ ಶ್ಲೋಕಃ ಮಂತ್ರಃ

There is this Vedic verse

  • ಏಷಃ → this
  • ಶ್ಲೋಕಃ → verse
  • ಮಂತ್ರಃ → mantra

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text:
ತಾನ್ಹ ಸ ಋಷಿರುವಾಚ ಭೂಯ ಏವ ತಪಸಾ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾನ್ಪೃಚ್ಛತ ಯದಿ ವಿಜ್ಞಾಸ್ಯಾಮಃ ಸರ್ವಂ ಹ ವೋ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮ ಇತಿ ॥ ೨ ॥ To them, the sage said: "Live here for one more year, practicing austerity, brahmacarya, and faith. Then ask questions according to your desire. If we know the answers, we shall explain everything to you."

ತಾನ್ ಹ — to them indeed

  • ತಾನ್ → to them
  • ಹ → indeed

ಸ ಋಷಿಃ ಉವಾಚ — the sage said

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಋಷಿಃ → the sage
  • ಉವಾಚ → said

ಭೂಯ ಏವ — for some more time; further

  • ಭೂಯಃ → further, additional
  • ಏವ → indeed

ತಪಸಾ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ — through austerity, brahmacarya, and faith

  • ತಪಸಾ → through austerity
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ → through brahmacarya
  • ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ → through faith

ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ — you shall stay for a year

  • ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ → for one year
  • ಸಂವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ → you shall stay, dwell

ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾನ್ ಪೃಚ್ಛತ — ask questions according to your desire

  • ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ → according to your wish
  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾನ್ → questions
  • ಪೃಚ್ಛತ → ask

ಯದಿ ವಿಜ್ಞಾಸ್ಯಾಮಃ — if we know

  • ಯದಿ → if
  • ವಿಜ್ಞಾಸ್ಯಾಮಃ → we know

ಸರ್ವಂ ಹ ವಃ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಃ — we shall indeed tell you everything

  • ಸರ್ವಂ → everything
  • ಹ → indeed
  • ವಃ → to you
  • ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಃ → we shall tell

ಇತಿ — thus

  • ಇತಿ → thus

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text:
ತಾನ್ ಏವಮುಪಗತಾನ್ ಸಃ ಹ ಕಿಲ ಋಷಿಃ ಉವಾಚ ಭೂಯಃ ಪುನರೇವ — ಯದ್ಯಪಿ ಯೂಯಂ ಪೂರ್ವಂ ತಪಸ್ವಿನ ಏವ, ತಥಾಪೀಹ ತಪಸಾ ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಸಂಯಮೇನ ವಿಶೇಷತೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ ಚ ಆಸ್ತಿಕ್ಯಬುದ್ಧ್ಯಾ ಆದರವಂತಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ ಕಾಲಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ ಸಮ್ಯಗ್ಗುರುಶುಶ್ರೂಷಾಪರಾಃ ಸಂತೋ ವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ । ತತಃ ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ ಯೋ ಯಸ್ಯ ಕಾಮಸ್ತಮನತಿಕ್ರಮ್ಯ ಯದ್ವಿಷಯೇ ಯಸ್ಯ ಜಿಜ್ಞಾಸಾ ತದ್ವಿಷಯಾನ್ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾನ್ ಪೃಚ್ಛತ । ಯದಿ ತದ್ಯುಷ್ಮತ್ಪೃಷ್ಟಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾಸ್ಯಾಮಃ । ಅನುದ್ಧತತ್ವಪ್ರದರ್ಶನಾರ್ಥೋ ಯದಿ - ಶಬ್ದೋ ನಾಜ್ಞಾನಸಂಶಯಾರ್ಥಃ ಪ್ರಶ್ನನಿರ್ಣಯಾದವಸೀಯತೇ ಸರ್ವಂ ಹ ವೋ ವಃ ಪೃಷ್ಟಾರ್ಥಂ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮ ಇತಿ ॥ To those who had approached him in that manner, the sage indeed said again: "Although you are already practitioners of austerity, nevertheless, remain here for a year with discipline — practicing austerity in the form of control of the senses, especially brahmacarya, and faith, that is, a trusting attitude toward the authority of the scriptures and the teacher. Live here with reverence and with wholehearted dedication to serving the teacher. Thereafter, ask questions according to your respective desires. Whatever subject each of you wishes to know, and whatever inquiry arises in each one's mind, ask questions concerning that very subject. If we know the answer to what you ask, we shall explain it to you." The word 'if' (yadi) is used only to indicate the sage's humility and freedom from arrogance; it is not intended to imply ignorance or doubt. This is evident from the fact that all the questions are subsequently answered and resolved. Thus he says: "We shall indeed explain to you everything concerning the matters that you ask."

ತಾನ್ ಏವಮ್ ಉಪಗತಾನ್ ಸಃ ಹ ಕಿಲ ಋಷಿಃ ಉವಾಚ

The sage indeed said to those who had approached him in this manner.

  • ತಾನ್ → those (students)
  • ಏವಮ್ → thus, in this manner
  • ಉಪಗತಾನ್ → those who had approached
  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಹ ಕಿಲ → indeed
  • ಋಷಿಃ → the sage
  • ಉವಾಚ → said

ಭೂಯಃ ಪುನರೇವ

Further, once again.

  • ಭೂಯಃ → further, additionally
  • ಪುನಃ → again
  • ಏವ → indeed

ಯದ್ಯಪಿ ಯೂಯಂ ಪೂರ್ವಂ ತಪಸ್ವಿನ ಏವ

Although you are already practitioners of austerity,

  • ಯದ್ಯಪಿ → although
  • ಯೂಯಂ → you
  • ಪೂರ್ವಂ → previously, already
  • ತಪಸ್ವಿನಃ → practitioners of austerity
  • ಏವ → indeed

ತಥಾಪಿ ಇಹ ತಪಸಾ ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಸಂಯಮೇನ

Even so, here through tapas, namely control of the senses,

  • ತಥಾಪಿ → nevertheless
  • ಇಹ → here
  • ತಪಸಾ → through austerity
  • ಇಂದ್ರಿಯ-ಸಂಯಮೇನ → through restraint of the senses
  • ಇಂದ್ರಿಯ → senses
  • ಸಂಯಮ → control, restraint
  • ಏನ → by, through

Śaṅkara explicitly glosses tapas here as indriya-saṃyama (sense-control).

ವಿಶೇಷತೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ

Especially through brahmacarya.

  • ವಿಶೇಷತಃ → especially, particularly
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ → through brahmacarya

ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ ಚ ಆಸ್ತಿಕ್ಯಬುದ್ಧ್ಯಾ

And through faith, that is, a trusting attitude toward the scriptures and teacher.

  • ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ → through faith
  • ಚ → and
  • ಆಸ್ತಿಕ್ಯ-ಬುದ್ಧ್ಯಾ → through an attitude of trust in the authority of the scriptures
  • ಆಸ್ತಿಕ್ಯ → faith in the validity of the Veda
  • ಬುದ್ಧಿ → understanding, attitude

ಆದರವಂತಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ ಕಾಲಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ

You shall live here for a year with reverence.

  • ಆದರ-ವಂತಃ → possessed of reverence
  • ಆದರ → respect, reverence
  • ವಂತಃ → possessing
  • ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ ಕಾಲಂ → for the period of one year
  • ಸಂವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ → you shall stay

ಸಮ್ಯಕ್ ಗುರುಶುಶ್ರೂಷಾಪರಾಃ ಸಂತಃ ವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ

You shall live devoted to proper service of the teacher.

  • ಸಮ್ಯಕ್ → properly
  • ಗುರು-ಶುಶ್ರೂಷಾ-ಪರಾಃ → devoted to service of the teacher
  • ಗುರು → teacher
  • ಶುಶ್ರೂಷಾ → service, attendance
  • ಪರಾಃ → dedicated to
  • ಸಂತಃ → being
  • ವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ → you shall live

ತತಃ ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ

Thereafter, according to your desire,

  • ತತಃ → then, thereafter
  • ಯಥಾ-ಕಾಮಂ → according to your wish

ಯಃ ಯಸ್ಯ ಕಾಮಃ ತಂ ಅನತಿಕ್ರಮ್ಯ

Without going beyond what each one desires to know.

  • ಯಃ → whichever
  • ಯಸ್ಯ → of whom
  • ಕಾಮಃ → desire
  • ತಂ → that
  • ಅನತಿಕ್ರಮ್ಯ → not transgressing, not exceeding

ಯದ್ವಿಷಯೇ ಯಸ್ಯ ಜಿಜ್ಞಾಸಾ

Regarding whatever subject each one has an inquiry,

  • ಯದ್-ವಿಷಯೇ → regarding whichever topic
  • ಯಸ್ಯ → of whom
  • ಜಿಜ್ಞಾಸಾ → desire to know, inquiry

ತದ್ವಿಷಯಾನ್ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾನ್ ಪೃಚ್ಛತ

Ask questions concerning those subjects.

  • ತದ್-ವಿಷಯಾನ್ → concerning those subjects
  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾನ್ → questions
  • ಪೃಚ್ಛತ → ask

ಯದಿ ತತ್ ಯುಷ್ಮತ್ ಪೃಷ್ಟಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾಸ್ಯಾಮಃ

If we know that which is asked by you,

  • ಯದಿ → if
  • ತತ್ → that
  • ಯುಷ್ಮತ್-ಪೃಷ್ಟಂ → asked by you
  • ಯುಷ್ಮತ್ → by you
  • ಪೃಷ್ಟಂ → asked
  • ವಿಜ್ಞಾಸ್ಯಾಮಃ → we know

ಅನುದ್ಧತತ್ವಪ್ರದರ್ಶನಾರ್ಥಃ ಯದಿ-ಶಬ್ದಃ

The word "if" is used to indicate absence of arrogance.

  • ಅನುದ್ಧತತ್ವ-ಪ್ರದರ್ಶನಾರ್ಥಃ → for demonstrating humility
  • ಅನುದ್ಧತತ್ವ → non-arrogance, humility
  • ಪ್ರದರ್ಶನ → showing
  • ಅರ್ಥಃ → purpose
  • ಯದಿ-ಶಬ್ದಃ → the word "if"

This is an important observation of Śaṅkara.

ನ ಅಜ್ಞಾನಸಂಶಯಾರ್ಥಃ

It is not intended to suggest ignorance or doubt.

  • ನ → not
  • ಅಜ್ಞಾನ → ignorance
  • ಸಂಶಯ → doubt
  • ಅರ್ಥಃ → meaning, purpose
  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನನಿರ್ಣಯಾತ್ ಅವಸೀಯತೇ

This is understood from the subsequent resolution of the questions.

  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನ-ನಿರ್ಣಯಾತ್ → from the determination of the questions
  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನ → questions
  • ನಿರ್ಣಯ → ascertainment, resolution
  • ಅವಸೀಯತೇ → is understood, is concluded

ಸರ್ವಂ ಹ ವಃ ಪೃಷ್ಟಾರ್ಥಂ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಃ ಇತಿ

"We shall indeed explain to you everything that you ask."

  • ಸರ್ವಂ → everything
  • ಹ → indeed
  • ವಃ → to you
  • ಪೃಷ್ಟ-ಅರ್ಥಂ → the matter asked about
  • ಪೃಷ್ಟ → asked
  • ಅರ್ಥಂ → subject matter
  • ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಃ → we shall explain
  • ಇತಿ → thus

ಅಥ — then

  • ಅಥ → then, thereafter

ಕಬಂಧೀ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ — Kabandhī, the son of Kātyāyana

  • ಕಬಂಧೀ → Kabandhī
  • ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ → descendant of Kātyāyana

ಉಪೇತ್ಯ — having approached

  • ಉಪೇತ್ಯ → having approached, having come near

ಪಪ್ರಚ್ಛ — asked

  • ಪಪ್ರಚ್ಛ → asked, inquired

ಭಗವನ್ — O Revered Sir

  • ಭಗವನ್ → O venerable one, revered teacher

ಕುತಃ ಹ ವಾ — from where indeed

  • ಕುತಃ → from where
  • ಹ → indeed
  • ವಾ → verily, surely

  • ಇಮಾಃ → these
  • ಪ್ರಜಾಃ → beings, living creatures, progeny

  • ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತೇ → are produced, are born

docs.text:
ಅಥ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಾದೂರ್ಧ್ವಂ ಕಬಂಧೀ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ ಉಪೇತ್ಯ ಉಪಗಮ್ಯ ಪಪ್ರಚ್ಛ ಪೃಷ್ಟವಾನ್ — ಹೇ ಭಗವನ್ , ಕುತಃ ಕಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಹ ವೈ ಇಮಾಃ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಾದ್ಯಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತೇ ಉತ್ಪದ್ಯಂತೇ ಇತಿ । ಅಪರವಿದ್ಯಾಕರ್ಮಣೋಃ ಸಮುಚ್ಚಿತಯೋರ್ಯತ್ಕಾರ್ಯಂ ಯಾ ಗತಿಸ್ತದ್ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಮಿತಿ ತದರ್ಥೋಽಯಂ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಃ ॥ Then, after the completion of the year, Kabandhī Kātyāyana approached the teacher and asked: "O Revered Sir, from what cause indeed are these beings, beginning with the brāhmaṇas, born?" This question is intended to elicit an explanation of the result and destination attained through the combined pursuit of aparā vidyā (lower knowledge) and karma (Vedic rituals).

ಅಥ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಾದೂರ್ಧ್ವಂ

Then, after the completion of the year,

  • ಅಥ → then
  • ಸಂವತ್ಸರಾತ್ → from the year, after the year
  • ಊರ್ಧ್ವಂ → afterwards, subsequently

ಕಬಂಧೀ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ ಉಪೇತ್ಯ ಉಪಗಮ್ಯ

Kabandhī Kātyāyana, having approached the teacher,

  • ಕಬಂಧೀ → Kabandhī
  • ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ → descendant of Kātyāyana
  • ಉಪೇತ್ಯ → having approached
  • ಉಪಗಮ್ಯ → having come near

Śaṅkara uses both expressions simply to emphasize respectful approach to the teacher.

ಪಪ್ರಚ್ಛ ಪೃಷ್ಟವಾನ್

Asked, inquired

  • ಪಪ್ರಚ್ಛ → asked
  • ಪೃಷ್ಟವಾನ್ → one who questioned

ಹೇ ಭಗವನ್

O Revered Sir,

  • ಹೇ → O!
  • ಭಗವನ್ → venerable master

ಕುತಃ ಕಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಹ ವೈ

From what cause indeed?

  • ಕುತಃ → from where
  • ಕಸ್ಮಾತ್ → from what cause
  • ಹ ವೈ → indeed, verily

Śaṅkara glosses ಕುತಃ with ಕಸ್ಮಾತ್, making it clear that the inquiry concerns the cause of creation.

ಇಮಾಃ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಾದ್ಯಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ

These beings, beginning with the brāhmaṇas,

  • ಇಮಾಃ → these
  • ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣ-ಆದ್ಯಾಃ → beginning with the brāhmaṇas
  • ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣ → brāhmaṇa
  • ಆದ್ಯಾಃ → and others, beginning with
  • ಪ್ರಜಾಃ → creatures, beings

Here "brāhmaṇas and others" stands for all embodied beings.

ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತೇ ಉತ್ಪದ್ಯಂತೇ

Are born, come into existence

  • ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತೇ → are born
  • ಉತ್ಪದ್ಯಂತೇ → arise, are produced

The second word is explanatory of the first.

ಅಪರವಿದ್ಯಾಕರ್ಮಣೋಃ ಸಮುಚ್ಚಿತಯೋಃ

Of aparā vidyā and karma taken together,

  • ಅಪರ-ವಿದ್ಯಾ → lower knowledge (primarily Vedic learning)
  • ಕರ್ಮಣೋಃ → of karma
  • ಸಮುಚ್ಚಿತಯೋಃ → when combined together

This is a very important phrase.

ಯತ್ ಕಾರ್ಯಂ

What result is produced,

  • ಯತ್ → whatever
  • ಕಾರ್ಯಂ → effect, result

ಯಾ ಗತಿಃ

What destination is attained,

  • ಯಾ → what
  • ಗತಿಃ → destination, course, attainment

ತತ್ ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಂ ಇತಿ

That is what is to be explained.

  • ತತ್ → that
  • ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಂ → should be explained
  • ಇತಿ → thus

ತದರ್ಥಃ ಅಯಂ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಃ

Such is the intention of this question.

  • ತದರ್ಥಃ → having that purpose
  • ಅಯಂ → this
  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನಃ → question

Important Bhāṣya Point

At first glance, Kabandhī appears to be asking a simple cosmological question:

"From where are beings born?"

But Śaṅkara sees a deeper intention.

The question is really:

"What is the origin, result, and destination of the world experienced by those who pursue Vedic learning and ritual action?"

In other words, the inquiry is not merely about physical birth. It is about the creation-order (sṛṣṭi) that forms the field in which karma operates and produces results.

Therefore Śaṅkara remarks:

ಅಪರವಿದ್ಯಾಕರ್ಮಣೋಃ ಸಮುಚ್ಚಿತಯೋಃ ಯತ್ ಕಾರ್ಯಂ ಯಾ ಗತಿಃ

"The question seeks to know the result and destination associated with the combined pursuit of aparā vidyā and karma."

This prepares the way for Pippalāda's answer concerning Prajāpati, Rayi, and Prāṇa, which explains the cosmic order governing worldly existence.

ತಸ್ಮೈ ಸ ಹೋವಾಚ ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮೋ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಸ ತಪೋಽತಪ್ಯತ ಸ ತಪಸ್ತಪ್ತ್ವಾ ಸ ಮಿಥುನಮುತ್ಪಾದಯತೇ ರಯಿಂ ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಚೇತ್ಯೇತೌ ಮೇ ಬಹುಧಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತ ಇತಿ ॥ ೪ ॥ To him, the sage replied: "Prajāpati, desiring progeny, performed austerity. Having practiced austerity, he produced a pair — Rayi and Prāṇa — thinking, 'These two will create many kinds of beings for me.'"

ತಸ್ಮೈ ಸಃ ಹ ಉವಾಚ

To him indeed he said

  • ತಸ್ಮೈ → to him
  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಹ → indeed
  • ಉವಾಚ → said

ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಃ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ

Prajāpati indeed desired progeny

  • ಪ್ರಜಾ-ಕಾಮಃ → desirous of progeny
  • ಪ್ರಜಾ → offspring, beings
  • ಕಾಮಃ → desire
  • ವೈ → indeed
  • ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ → Prajāpati, the creator

ಸಃ ತಪಃ ಅತಪ್ಯತ

He practiced austerity

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ತಪಃ → austerity
  • ಅತಪ್ಯತ → practiced austerity

ಸಃ ತಪಃ ತಪ್ತ್ವಾ

Having performed austerity

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ತಪಃ → austerity
  • ತಪ್ತ್ವಾ → having practiced, having performed

ಸಃ ಮಿಥುನಂ ಉತ್ಪಾದಯತೇ

He produced a pair

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಮಿಥುನಂ → pair, couple
  • ಉತ್ಪಾದಯತೇ → produced, created

ರಯಿಂ ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಚ

Rayi and Prāṇa

  • ರಯಿಂ → Rayi
  • ಚ → and
  • ಪ್ರಾಣಂ → Prāṇa
  • ಚ → and

ಇತಿ ಏತೌ ಮೇ ಬಹುಧಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಃ

"These two will create many kinds of beings for me"

  • ಇತಿ → thus
  • ಏತೌ → these two
  • ಮೇ → for me
  • ಬಹುಧಾ → in many ways, manifoldly
  • ಪ್ರಜಾಃ → beings, offspring
  • ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಃ → will create, will produce

ಇತಿ

Thus

  • ಇತಿ → thus

ತಸ್ಮೈ ಏವಂ ಪೃಷ್ಟವತೇ ಸ ಹ ಉವಾಚ ತದಪಾಕರಣಾಯಾಹ — ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಆತ್ಮನಃ ಸಿಸೃಕ್ಷುಃ ವೈ, ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾ ಸನ್ ಜಗತ್ಸ್ರಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮೀತ್ಯೇವಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನವಾನ್ಯಥೋಕ್ತಕಾರೀ ತದ್ಭಾವಭಾವಿತಃ ಕಲ್ಪಾದೌ ನಿರ್ವೃತ್ತೋ ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭಃ, ಸೃಜ್ಯಮಾನಾನಾಂ ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಂ ಸ್ಥಾವರಜಂಗಮಾನಾಂ ಪತಿಃ ಸನ್ , ಜನ್ಮಾಂತರಭಾವಿತಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಂ ಶ್ರುತಿಪ್ರಕಾಶಿತಾರ್ಥವಿಷಯಂ ತಪಃ, ಅನ್ವಾಲೋಚಯತ್ ಅತಪ್ಯತ । ಅಥ ತು ಸಃ ಏವಂ ತಪಃ ತಪ್ತ್ವಾ ಶ್ರೌತಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಮನ್ವಾಲೋಚ್ಯ, ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಸಾಧನಭೂತಂ ಮಿಥುನಮ್ ಉತ್ಪಾದಯತೇ ಮಿಥುನಂ ದ್ವಂದ್ವಮುತ್ಪಾದಿತವಾನ್ ರಯಿಂ ಚ ಸೋಮಮನ್ನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಚ ಅಗ್ನಿಮತ್ತಾರಮ್ ಇತ್ಯೇತೌ ಅಗ್ನೀಷೋಮೌ ಅತ್ರನ್ನಭೂತೌ ಮೇ ಮಮ ಬಹುಧಾ ಅನೇಕಧಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಃ ಇತಿ ಏವಂ ಸಂಚಿಂತ್ಯ ಅಂಡೋತ್ಪತ್ತಿಕ್ರಮೇಣ ಸೂರ್ಯಾಚಂದ್ರಮಸಾವಕಲ್ಪಯತ್ ॥ To him who had asked in this manner, Pippalāda replied in order to remove his doubt. Prajāpati, desiring to create beings from himself, being the Self of all and endowed with the knowledge, "I shall create the universe," and acting in accordance with that knowledge, manifested as Hiraṇyagarbha at the beginning of a cycle of creation. As the lord of all beings that were to be created, both stationary and moving, he contemplated upon tapas, which here means knowledge concerning the truths revealed by the scriptures and carried forward from previous births. Having thus practiced that tapas, and having reflected upon the scriptural knowledge, he created a pair which would serve as the means of creation. He produced the duality of Rayi and Prāṇa — Rayi being the Moon, food; and Prāṇa being Fire, the eater of food. Thinking, "These two, Agni and Soma, food and eater, will generate for me beings in many forms," he projected the Sun and Moon through the process of cosmic manifestation beginning from the cosmic egg.

ತಸ್ಮೈ ಏವಂ ಪೃಷ್ಟವತೇ

To him who had asked in this manner

  • ತಸ್ಮೈ → to him
  • ಏವಂ → thus, in this manner
  • ಪೃಷ್ಟವತೇ → to the one who had questioned

ಸಃ ಹ ಉವಾಚ

He indeed said

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಹ → indeed
  • ಉವಾಚ → said

ತದಪಾಕರಣಾಯ

For removing that doubt

  • ತತ್ → that
  • ಅಪಾಕರಣಾಯ → for removal, for clearing away

ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಆತ್ಮನಃ ಸಿಸೃಕ್ಷುಃ

Desiring to create beings from himself

  • ಪ್ರಜಾ-ಕಾಮಃ → desirous of creating beings
  • ಪ್ರಜಾಃ → beings
  • ಆತ್ಮನಃ → from himself (panchami vibhakthi)
  • ಸಿಸೃಕ್ಷುಃ → desirous of creating

ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ

Indeed Prajāpati

  • ವೈ → indeed
  • ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ → Prajāpati

ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾ ಸನ್

Being the Self of all

  • ಸರ್ವ → all
  • ಆತ್ಮಾ → Self
  • ಸನ್ → being

ಜಗತ್ ಸ್ರಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಿ ಇತಿ

"I shall create the universe"

  • ಜಗತ್ → universe
  • ಸ್ರಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಿ → I shall create
  • ಇತಿ → thus

ಏವಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನವಾನ್

Possessed of this knowledge

  • ಏವಂ → thus
  • ವಿಜ್ಞಾನವಾನ್ → endowed with knowledge

ಯಥೋಕ್ತಕಾರೀ

Acting in accordance with that knowledge

  • ಯಥಾ → according to
  • ಉಕ್ತ → what was known or understood
  • ಕಾರೀ → one who acts

ತದ್ಭಾವಭಾವಿತಃ

Endowed with that contemplation

  • ತತ್ → that
  • ಭಾವ → contemplation, idea
  • ಭಾವಿತಃ → imbued with, pervaded by

ಕಲ್ಪಾದೌ ನಿರ್ವೃತ್ತಃ ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭಃ

Manifested as Hiraṇyagarbha at the beginning of creation

  • ಕಲ್ಪ-ಆದೌ → at the beginning of a kalpa
  • ನಿರ್ವೃತ್ತಃ → manifested, came forth
  • ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭಃ → Hiraṇyagarbha

ಸೃಜ್ಯಮಾನಾನಾಂ ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಂ ಸ್ಥಾವರಜಂಗಮಾನಾಂ ಪತಿಃ ಸನ್

Being the lord of all beings to be created, moving and unmoving

  • ಸೃಜ್ಯಮಾನಾನಾಂ → of those being created
  • ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಂ → beings
  • ಸ್ಥಾವರ → stationary
  • ಜಂಗಮಾನಾಂ → moving
  • ಪತಿಃ → lord
  • ಸನ್ → being

ಜನ್ಮಾಂತರಭಾವಿತಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಂ

Knowledge carried over from previous births

  • ಜನ್ಮಾಂತರ → previous births
  • ಭಾವಿತಂ → cultivated, carried forward
  • ಜ್ಞಾನಂ → knowledge

ಶ್ರುತಿಪ್ರಕಾಶಿತಾರ್ಥವಿಷಯಂ ತಪಃ

Tapas consisting of knowledge of truths revealed by scripture

  • ಶ್ರುತಿ → scripture
  • ಪ್ರಕಾಶಿತ → revealed
  • ಅರ್ಥ → truth, meaning
  • ವಿಷಯಂ → concerning
  • ತಪಃ → tapas

ಅನ್ವಾಲೋಚಯತ್ ಅತಪ್ಯತ

He reflected upon; he practiced tapas

  • ಅನ್ವಾಲೋಚಯತ್ → contemplated
  • ಅತಪ್ಯತ → practiced tapas

ಅಥ ತು ಸಃ ಏವಂ ತಪಃ ತಪ್ತ್ವಾ

Then, having thus performed tapas

  • ಅಥ ತು → then indeed
  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಏವಂ → thus
  • ತಪಃ → tapas
  • ತಪ್ತ್ವಾ → having practiced

ಶ್ರೌತಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಂ ಅನ್ವಾಲೋಚ್ಯ

Having reflected upon scriptural knowledge

  • ಶ್ರೌತಂ → scriptural (told in the vedas)
  • ಜ್ಞಾನಂ → knowledge
  • ಅನ್ವಾಲೋಚ್ಯ → having contemplated

ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಸಾಧನಭೂತಂ ಮಿಥುನಮ್ ಉತ್ಪಾದಯತೇ

He produced a pair that would become the means of creation

  • ಸೃಷ್ಟಿ → creation
  • ಸಾಧನಭೂತಂ → serving as the means
  • ಮಿಥುನಂ → pair (duality)
  • ಉತ್ಪಾದಯತೇ → produced

ಮಿಥುನಂ ದ್ವಂದ್ವಮ್ ಉತ್ಪಾದಿತವಾನ್

He created a duality

  • ಮಿಥುನಂ → pair
  • ದ್ವಂದ್ವಂ → duality
  • ಉತ್ಪಾದಿತವಾನ್ → created

ರಯಿಂ ಚ ಸೋಮಮ್ ಅನ್ನಂ

Rayi, namely the Moon, which is food

  • ರಯಿಂ → Rayi
  • ಚ → and
  • ಸೋಮಂ → Moon (in the form of food)
  • ಅನ್ನಂ → food

ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಚ ಅಗ್ನಿಮ್ ಅತ್ತಾರಮ್

Prāṇa, namely Fire, the eater

  • ಪ್ರಾಣಂ → Prāṇa (in the form of fire)
  • ಚ → and
  • ಅಗ್ನಿಂ → Fire
  • ಅತ್ತಾರಂ → eater, consumer

ಇತಿ ಏತೌ ಅಗ್ನೀಷೋಮೌ

Thus these two are Agni and Soma

  • ಇತಿ → thus
  • ಏತೌ → these two
  • ಅಗ್ನೀಷೋಮೌ → Agni and Soma

ಅನ್ನಭೂತೌ

Food and eater (TODO CHECK) - Athru -> here --- CHECK - ಅನ್ನ → food - ಭೂತೌ → being

ಮೇ ಮಮ ಬಹುಧಾ ಅನೇಕಧಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಃ

Will create for me beings of many kinds

  • ಮೇ / ಮಮ → for me
  • ಬಹುಧಾ → manifoldly
  • ಅನೇಕಧಾ → in many ways
  • ಪ್ರಜಾಃ → beings
  • ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಃ → will create

ಇತಿ ಏವಂ ಸಂಚಿಂತ್ಯ

Having thus thought

  • ಇತಿ → thus
  • ಏವಂ → in this manner
  • ಸಂಚಿಂತ್ಯ → having reflected

ಅಂಡೋತ್ಪತ್ತಿಕ್ರಮೇಣ

Through the process of cosmic egg manifestation

  • ಅಂಡ → cosmic egg
  • ಉತ್ಪತ್ತಿ → origination
  • ಕ್ರಮೇಣ → in sequence

ಸೂರ್ಯಾಚಂದ್ರಮಸೌ ಅಕಲ್ಪಯತ್

He projected the Sun and Moon

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text: ತತ್ರ ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ ಹ ವೈ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅತ್ತಾ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ । ರಯಿರೇವ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾಃ । ರಯಿರೇವಾನ್ನಂ ಸೋಮ ಏವ । ತದೇತದೇಕಮತ್ತಾ ಅಗ್ನಿಶ್ಚಾನ್ನಂ ಚ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿರೇಕಂ ತು ಮಿಥುನಮ್ ; ಗುಣಪ್ರಧಾನಕೃತೋ ಭೇದಃ । ಕಥಮ್ ? ರಯಿರ್ವೈ ಅನ್ನಮೇವ ಏತತ್ ಸರ್ವಮ್ । ಕಿಂ ತತ್ ? ಯತ್ ಮೂರ್ತಂ ಚ ಸ್ಥೂಲಂ ಚ ಅಮೂರ್ತಂ ಚ ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮಂ ಚ । ಮೂರ್ತಾಮೂರ್ತೇ ಅತ್ತ್ರನ್ನರೂಪೇ ಅಪಿ ರಯಿರೇವ । ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಪ್ರವಿಭಕ್ತಾದಮೂರ್ತಾತ್ ಯದನ್ಯನ್ಮೂರ್ತರೂಪಂ ಮೂರ್ತಿಃ, ಸೈವ ರಯಿಃ ಅನ್ನಮ್ ಅಮೂರ್ತೇನ ಅತ್ತ್ರಾ ಅದ್ಯಮಾನತ್ವಾತ್ ॥   Among the two, the Sun is indeed Prāṇa, the eater, Fire. The Moon alone is Rayi. Rayi itself is food, that is, Soma.  Thus, the eater, Fire, and the food together constitute a single Prajāpati appearing as a pair. The distinction between them is made only on account of differences in attributes and predominance.  How so? Indeed, all this is nothing but Rayi, that is, food. What is that all? Whatever is gross and formed, and whatever is subtle and formless. Both the formed and the formless, though constituting the eater and the eaten, are still Rayi alone.  Therefore, among these, the formed aspect, distinguished from the formless, is specifically called Rayi or food, because it is consumed by the formless eater.

docs.text: ತಥಾ ಅಮೂರ್ತೋಽಪಿ ಪ್ರಾಣೋಽತ್ತಾ ಸರ್ವಮೇವ ಯಚ್ಚಾದ್ಯಮ್ । ಕಥಮ್ ? ಅಥ ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ ಉದಯನ್ ಉದ್ಗಚ್ಛನ್ ಪ್ರಾಣಿನಾಂ ಚಕ್ಷುರ್ಗೋಚರಮಾಗಚ್ಛನ್ ಯತ್ಪ್ರಾಚೀಂ ದಿಶಂ ಸ್ವಪ್ರಕಾಶೇನ ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ ವ್ಯಾಪ್ನೋತಿ, ತೇನ ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮವ್ಯಾಪ್ತ್ಯಾ ಸರ್ವಾಂತಃಸ್ಥಾನ್ ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್ ಪ್ರಾಚ್ಯಾನನ್ನಭೂತಾನ್ ರಶ್ಮಿಷು ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮಾವಭಾಸರೂಪೇಷು ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿಮತ್ಸು ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತತ್ವಾತ್ಪ್ರಾಣಿನಃ ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ ಸಂನಿವೇಶಯತಿ ಆತ್ಮಭೂತಾನ್ಕರೋತೀತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ । ತಥೈವ ಯತ್ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಂ ಯತ್ಪ್ರತೀಚೀಂ ಯದುದೀಚೀಮ್ ಅಧಃ ಊರ್ಧ್ವಂ ಯತ್ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ ಯಚ್ಚ ಅಂತರಾ ದಿಶಃ ಕೋಣದಿಶೋಽವಾಂತರದಿಶಃ ಯಚ್ಚಾನ್ಯತ್ ಸರ್ವಂ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಯತಿ, ತೇನ ಸ್ವಪ್ರಕಾಶವ್ಯಾಪ್ತ್ಯಾ ಸರ್ವಾನ್ ಸರ್ವದಿಕ್ಸ್ಥಾನ್ ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್ ರಶ್ಮಿಷು ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ ॥   Likewise, though Prāṇa is formless, it is the eater of everything that is fit to be eaten.  How is this so?  When the Sun rises and becomes visible to the eyes of living beings, and enters or pervades the eastern direction through its own light, by that pervasion it gathers into its rays all beings dwelling in the east, who are in the nature of food. Since the rays are pervaded by the Sun's own luminous presence, the beings are established in them. That is, the Sun makes them one with himself. When he enters the western direction

When he enters the northern direction

Below and above

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text: ಸ ಏಷ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರೋ ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಃ ಪ್ರಾಣೋಽಗ್ನಿರುದಯತೇ । ತದೇತದೃಚಾಭ್ಯುಕ್ತಮ್ ॥ ೭ ॥   This very Prāṇa, rising as the Sun, is Vaiśvānara, the cosmic Fire, of universal form. Concerning this, the following Ṛg-vedic mantra has been declared.

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ಸಃ ಏಷಃ

This very one

  • ಏಷಃ → this very one

ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ

Vaiśvānara, the universal Fire

  • ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ → the cosmic fire, Vaiśvānara

Of universal form

Prāṇa, as Fire, rises

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text: ಸ ಏಷಃ ಅತ್ತಾ ಪ್ರಾಣೋ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾ ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಃ ವಿಶ್ವಾತ್ಮತ್ವಾಚ್ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅಗ್ನಿಶ್ಚ ಸ ಏವಾತ್ತಾ ಉದಯತೇ ಉದ್ಗಚ್ಛತಿ ಪ್ರತ್ಯಹಂ ಸರ್ವಾ ದಿಶಃ ಆತ್ಮಸಾತ್ಕುರ್ವನ್ । ತದೇತತ್ ಉಕ್ತಂ ವಸ್ತು ಋಚಾ ಮಂತ್ರೇಣಾಪಿ ಅಭ್ಯುಕ್ತಮ್ ॥   This very Prāṇa, the eater, is Vaiśvānara, the Self of all, possessing the form of the entire universe. Because he is the Self of all, Prāṇa and Fire are one and the same. That very eater rises every day, ascending while bringing all directions under his sway.  This very truth that has been explained is also declared in a Ṛg-vedic mantra.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ಸಃ ಏಷಃ ಅತ್ತಾ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ

This very Prāṇa, the eater, is Vaiśvānara

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಏಷಃ → this very one
  • ಅತ್ತಾ → eater
  • ಪ್ರಾಣಃ → Prāṇa
  • ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ → Vaiśvānara, the universal Fire

ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾ ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಃ

The Self of all, possessing universal form

  • ಸರ್ವ → all
  • ಆತ್ಮಾ → Self
  • ವಿಶ್ವ → universe
  • ರೂಪಃ → form

ವಿಶ್ವಾತ್ಮತ್ವಾತ್ ಚ

And because he is the Self of the universe

  • ಆತ್ಮತ್ವಾತ್ → because of being the Self
  • ಚ → and

ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ಚ

Prāṇa and Fire

  • ಪ್ರಾಣಃ → Prāṇa
  • ಅಗ್ನಿಃ → Fire
  • ಚ → and

ಸಃ ಏವ ಅತ್ತಾ

That very one is the eater

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಏವ → indeed
  • ಅತ್ತಾ → eater

ಉದಯತೇ ಉದ್ಗಚ್ಛತಿ

Rises and ascends

  • ಉದಯತೇ → rises
  • ಉದ್ಗಚ್ಛತಿ → ascends

ಪ್ರತ್ಯಹಂ

Every day

  • ಪ್ರತಿ → each
  • ಅಹಂ → day

ಸರ್ವಾಃ ದಿಶಃ ಆತ್ಮಸಾತ್ಕುರ್ವನ್

Bringing all directions under himself

  • ಸರ್ವಾಃ → all
  • ದಿಶಃ → directions
  • ಆತ್ಮಸಾತ್-ಕುರ್ವನ್ → making his own, bringing under his control

ತತ್ ಏತತ್ ಉಕ್ತಂ ವಸ್ತು

This very truth that has been taught

  • ತತ್ → that
  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ಉಕ್ತಂ → spoken, taught
  • ವಸ್ತು → reality, subject matter

Has also been declared by a Vedic mantra

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text: ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಂ ಹರಿಣಂ ಜಾತವೇದಸಂ ಪರಾಯಣಂ ಜ್ಯೋತಿರೇಕಂ ತಪಂತಮ್ । ಸಹಸ್ರರಶ್ಮಿಃ ಶತಧಾ ವರ್ತಮಾನಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಮುದಯತ್ಯೇಷ ಸೂರ್ಯಃ ॥ ೮ ॥   This Sun, who is the Prāṇa of all beings, rises as the one light, the ultimate refuge, all-formed, radiant, all-knowing, shining brightly, possessing a thousand rays, and manifesting himself in hundreds of ways.

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಂ

Of universal form

ಹರಿಣಂ

Radiant, shining

  • ಹರಿಣಂ → shining, golden-hued, radiant

ಜಾತವೇದಸಂ

The all-knowing one

  • ಜಾತ → beings, things that are born
  • ವೇದಸಂ → knower
  • ಜಾತವೇದಸಂ → knower of all beings

ಪರಾಯಣಂ

The supreme refuge

  • ಪರ → supreme
  • ಆಯಣಂ → refuge, resting place

ಜ್ಯೋತಿಃ ಏಕಂ

The one light

  • ಜ್ಯೋತಿಃ → light
  • ಏಕಂ → one

ತಪಂತಮ್

Shining, heating

  • ತಪಂತಮ್ → blazing, shining forth

ಸಹಸ್ರರಶ್ಮಿಃ

Possessing a thousand rays

  • ಸಹಸ್ರ → thousand
  • ರಶ್ಮಿಃ → rays

The Prāṇa of all beings

Rises

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text: ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಂ ಸರ್ವರೂಪಂ ಹರಿಣಂ ರಶ್ಮಿವಂತಂ ಜಾತವೇದಸಂ ಜಾತಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾನಂ ಪರಾಯಣಂ ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಾಶ್ರಯಂ ಜ್ಯೋತಿಃ ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಿನಾಂ ಚಕ್ಷುರ್ಭೂತಮ್ ಏಕಮ್ ಅದ್ವಿತೀಯಂ ತಪಂತಂ ತಾಪಕ್ರಿಯಾಂ ಕುರ್ವಾಣಂ ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಸೂರ್ಯಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾತವಂತೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವಿದಃ । ಕೋಽಸೌ ಯಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾತವಂತಃ ? ಸಹಸ್ರರಶ್ಮಿಃ ಅನೇಕರಶ್ಮಿಃ ಶತಧಾ ಅನೇಕಧಾ ಪ್ರಾಣಿಭೇದೇನ ವರ್ತಮಾನಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಮ್ ಉದಯತಿ ಏಷಃ ಸೂರ್ಯಃ ॥   The knowers of Brahman understand the Sun as their very Self — the one who has all forms, who is radiant with rays, who knows all beings, who is the refuge of all, who is the light, who serves as the eye of all living beings, who is one without a second, and who shines by performing the function of giving heat and light.  Who is that Sun whom they thus realize?  He is the one possessing countless rays, manifesting in many ways through the diversity of living beings. This very Sun rises as the Prāṇa, the life-principle of all creatures.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಂ ಸರ್ವರೂಪಂ

  • ಸರ್ವರೂಪಂ → possessing all forms

The knower of all beings

  • ಜಾತಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾನಂ → aware of all creatures

ಪರಾಯಣಂ ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಾಶ್ರಯಂ

The supreme refuge and support of all beings

  • ಪರಾಯಣಂ → ultimate refuge
  • ಸರ್ವ-ಪ್ರಾಣ-ಆಶ್ರಯಂ → support of all living beings

ಜ್ಯೋತಿಃ ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಿನಾಂ ಚಕ್ಷುರ್ಭೂತಮ್

ಏಕಮ್ ಅದ್ವಿತೀಯಂ

  • ಏಕಮ್ → one

ತಪಂತಂ ತಾಪಕ್ರಿಯಾಂ ಕುರ್ವಾಣಂ

Shining and performing the act of heating

  • ತಾಪ-ಕ್ರಿಯಾಂ → the act of heating

The Sun as one's own Self

ವಿಜ್ಞಾತವಂತಃ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವಿದಃ

The knowers of Brahman have realized

  • ವಿಜ್ಞಾತವಂತಃ → have known, realized
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವಿದಃ → knowers of Brahman

ಕಃ ಅಸೌ ಯಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾತವಂತಃ

Who is that whom they have realized?

  • ಕಃ → who
  • ಅಸೌ → that
  • ಯಂ → whom
  • ವಿಜ್ಞಾತವಂತಃ → have realized

ಸಹಸ್ರರಶ್ಮಿಃ ಅನೇಕರಶ್ಮಿಃ

Possessing countless rays

  • ಸಹಸ್ರರಶ್ಮಿಃ → thousand-rayed
  • ಅನೇಕರಶ್ಮಿಃ → having many rays

ಶತಧಾ ಅನೇಕಧಾ

Manifesting in many ways

  • ಶತಧಾ → in hundreds of ways
  • ಅನೇಕಧಾ → in many ways

ಪ್ರಾಣಿಭೇದೇನ ವರ್ತಮಾನಃ

Existing through the diversity of living beings

  • ಪ್ರಾಣಿ → living being
  • ಭೇದೇನ → through distinctions
  • ವರ್ತಮಾನಃ → manifesting, existing

ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಂ

The life-principle of all creatures

  • ಪ್ರಾಣಃ → Prāṇa
  • ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಂ → of beings

This Sun rises

docs.title: ಮೂಲ (Mūla)
docs.text:
ಸಂವತ್ಸರೋ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಸ್ತಸ್ಯಾಯನೇ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ಚೋತ್ತರಂ ಚ ।

ತದ್ಯೇ ಹ ವೈ ತದಿಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತೇ ಕೃತಮಿತ್ಯುಪಾಸತೇ ತೇ ಚಾಂದ್ರಮಸಮೇವ ಲೋಕಮಭಿಜಯಂತೇ ।

ತ ಏವ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಂತೇ ತಸ್ಮಾದೇತ ಋಷಯಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಾ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ ।

ಏಷ ಹ ವೈ ರಯಿರ್ಯಃ ಪಿತೃಯಾಣಃ ॥ ೯ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text: The Year (Saṃvatsara) is indeed Prajāpati (the Lord of creatures). His two paths are the Southern and the Northern. Those who worship iṣṭa (sacrificial rites) and pūrta (charitable works) as the (sufficient) accomplishment — they win only the lunar world. They indeed return again (to this world). Therefore those seers who desire progeny resort to the Southern path. This very Pitṛyāṇa is Rayi (the material/nourishing principle).

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya)

ಯಶ್ಚಾಸೌ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾ ಮೂರ್ತಿರನ್ನಮಮೂರ್ತಿಶ್ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣೋಽತ್ತಾದಿತ್ಯಸ್ತದೇತದೇಕಂ ಮಿಥುನಂ ಸರ್ವಂ ಕಥಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತ ಇತಿ, ಉಚ್ಯತೇ — ತದೇವ ಕಾಲಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರೋ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ, ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ ।

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತಿಥ್ಯಹೋರಾತ್ರಸಮುದಾಯೋ ಹಿ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ ತದನನ್ಯತ್ವಾದ್ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣೈತನ್ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕ ಏವೇತ್ಯುಚ್ಯತೇ ।

ತತ್ಕಥಮ್ ? ತಸ್ಯ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತೇಃ ಅಯನೇ ಮಾರ್ಗೌ ದ್ವೌ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ಚೋತ್ತರಂ ಚ ।

ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧೇ ಹ್ಯಯನೇ ಷಣ್ಮಾಸಲಕ್ಷಣೇ, ಯಾಭ್ಯಾಂ ದಕ್ಷಿಣೇನೋತ್ತರೇಣ ಚ ಯಾತಿ ಸವಿತಾ ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಸಂಯುಕ್ತಕರ್ಮವತಾಂ ಚ ಲೋಕಾನ್ವಿದಧತ್ ।

ಕಥಮ್ ? ತತ್ ತತ್ರ ಚ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಾದಿಷು ಯೇ ಹ ವೈ ಋಷಯಃ ತದುಪಾಸತ ಇತಿ ।

ಕ್ರಿಯಾವಿಶೇಷಣೋ ದ್ವಿತೀಯಸ್ತಚ್ಛಬ್ದಃ ।

ಇಷ್ಟಂ ಚ ಪೂರ್ತಂ ಚ ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತೇ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ಕೃತಮೇವೋಪಾಸತೇ ನಾಕೃತಂ ನಿತ್ಯಮ್, ತೇ ಚಾಂದ್ರಮಸಮೇವ ಚಂದ್ರಮಸಿ ಭವಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತೇರ್ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕಸ್ಯಾಂಶಂ ರಯಿಮನ್ನಭೂತಂ ಲೋಕಮ್ ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ ಕೃತರೂಪತ್ವಾಚ್ಚಾಂದ್ರಮಸಸ್ಯ ।

ತೇ ಏವ ಚ ಕೃತಕ್ಷಯಾತ್ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಂತೇ ಇಮಂ ಲೋಕಂ ಹೀನತರಂ ವಾ ವಿಶಂತೀತಿ ಹ್ಯುಕ್ತಮ್ ।

ಯಸ್ಮಾದೇವಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಮನ್ನಾತ್ಮಕಂ ಫಲತ್ವೇನಾಭಿನಿರ್ವರ್ತಯಂತಿ ಚಂದ್ರಮಿಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತಕರ್ಮಣಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾರ್ಥಿನಃ ಏತೇ ಋಷಯಃ ಸ್ವರ್ಗದ್ರಷ್ಟಾರಃ ಗೃಹಸ್ಥಾಃ, ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ಸ್ವಕೃತಮೇವ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನೋಪಲಕ್ಷಿತಂ ಚಂದ್ರಂ ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ ।

ಏಷ ಹ ವೈ ರಯಿಃ ಅನ್ನಮ್, ಯಃ ಪಿತೃಯಾಣಃ ಪಿತೃಯಾಣೋಪಲಕ್ಷಿತಶ್ಚಂದ್ರಃ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
[Opening question — pūrvapakṣa:] The Moon is what has form (mūrti); food is matter; the formless (amūrti) is Prāṇa; and the Sun is the eater — how can this one pair generate all progeny?

[Answer:] It is said thus: That very Kāla (Time) is the Saṃvatsara, and the Saṃvatsara is indeed Prajāpati — because everything is produced out of it. For the Year is nothing but the aggregate of tithis (lunar days), days, and nights, produced by Moon and Sun together. Since the Year is non-different from the dyad of Rayi and Prāṇa, it is said to be of the very nature of that pair (mithunātmaka).

How so? Prajāpati the Year has two paths — the Southern and the Northern. These are the well-known solstices (ayanas), each characterised by six months, by which the Sun (Savitṛ) travels southward and northward, distributing worlds respectively to those who perform only ritual action (kevalakarmins) and to those who combine knowledge with action (jñānasaṃyuktakarmavants).

How exactly? Among Brāhmaṇas and others — those seers who worship the iṣṭāpūrta as accomplished. The second occurrence of the word "tat" here serves as an adjective qualifying the action. Iṣṭa is sacrificial rite; pūrta is charitable work (and so on); they worship only what has been done (kṛtam) — not what is eternal and unconditioned (nitya). They win only the cāndramasa (lunar) world — the Rayi portion, the food-natured, material aspect of Prajāpati's dyadic nature, which exists in the Moon — because the lunar world has the character of the accomplished (kṛtarūpa).

They indeed return again when their accumulated merit is exhausted — entering this world or a still lower one, as has been stated. Because those seers — householders and perceivers of heaven — desire progeny and produce Prajāpati in his food-form as their fruit through sacrificial and charitable rites, they resort to the Southern path signified by the Southern solstice, which is nothing but the result of their own deeds. This Pitṛyāṇa is verily Rayi — food/matter. The Moon, characterised by the Pitṛyāṇa path, is that Rayi.

docs.title: Anvaya (Prose Order of the Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
The Bhāṣya contains four sentences whose word-order is sufficiently compressed or inverted that the syntactic structure needs to be laid out explicitly. These are the four that Ānandagiri himself flags with "ಇತ್ಯನ್ವಯಃ."

Sentence 1 — The pūrvapakṣa (opening question)

As written:

ಯಃ ಚಾಸೌ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾ ಮೂರ್ತಿಃ ಅನ್ನಂ ಅಮೂರ್ತಿಃ ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅತ್ತಾ ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ — ತತ್ ಏತತ್ ಏಕಂ ಮಿಥುನಂ ಸರ್ವಂ — ಕಥಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಿ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

ಯಃ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾ ಅಸೌ [ಸಃ] ಮೂರ್ತಿಃ [ರಯಿಃ] ; ಅನ್ನಂ [ಅಪಿ ರಯಿಃ ಏವ] ।

ಯಃ ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ [ಸಃ] ಅಮೂರ್ತಿಃ ; ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ [ಅಪಿ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಏವ,] ಅತ್ತಾ [ಚ] ।

ತತ್ ಏತತ್ [ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣರೂಪಂ] ಏಕಂ ಮಿಥುನಂ ಸರ್ವಂ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಕಂ [ಅಸ್ತಿ] ।

[ಏತತ್ ಮಿಥುನಂ] ಕಥಂ [ಸರ್ವಾಃ] ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಿ [ಇತಿ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಃ] ?

English: That Moon is the formed one (Rayi); food too is Rayi. That Prāṇa is the formless one; the Sun too is Prāṇa, and is the eater. That one pair — of the nature of Rayi and Prāṇa — is all, is everything. [Question:] How will this pair generate all progeny?

Sentence 2 — The Year produces through tithis and ahorātras

As written:

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯ-ತಿಥ್ಯಹೋರಾತ್ರ-ಸಮುದಾಯಃ ಹಿ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ ।

ತದನನ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣ-ಏತನ್ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕ ಏವ [ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ] ಇತಿ ಉಚ್ಯತೇ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ ಹಿ [ಕಃ ?] ಚಂದ್ರನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯ-ತಿಥಿ-ಆದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯ-ಅಹೋರಾತ್ರ-ಸಮುದಾಯಃ [ಏವ] ।

[ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ] ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣ-ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ [ಅನನ್ಯಃ] — ತದ್-ಅನನ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ — [ಅತಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ] ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕ ಏವ ಇತಿ ಉಚ್ಯತೇ ।

English: For what is the Year? It is the aggregate of the tithis produced by the Moon and the ahorātras (days-and-nights) produced by the Sun. Since the Year is non-different from the Rayi-Prāṇa pair — because of that non-difference — the Year is said to be of the very nature of that pair.

Note: The compound ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯ-ತಿಥ್ಯಹೋರಾತ್ರ-ಸಮುದಾಯಃ hides the internal division that Ānandagiri makes explicit: tithis are produced by the Moon, ahorātras by the Sun — not both by both.

Sentence 3 — The Sun's two movements and the worlds allotted (the most complex sentence)

As written:

ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧೇ ಹಿ ಅಯನೇ ಷಣ್ಮಾಸ-ಲಕ್ಷಣೇ, ಯಾಭ್ಯಾಂ ದಕ್ಷಿಣೇನ ಉತ್ತರೇಣ ಚ ಯಾತಿ ಸವಿತಾ ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಸಂಯುಕ್ತಕರ್ಮವತಾಂ ಚ ಲೋಕಾನ್ ವಿದಧತ್ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order — two separate syntactic streams):

[Stream 1 — Southern path:] ಸವಿತಾ [ಚಂದ್ರಃ ಅಪಿ — ಉಪಲಕ್ಷಣಾತ್] ದಕ್ಷಿಣೇನ [ಅಯನೇನ] ಯಾತಿ ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಲೋಕಾನ್ ವಿದಧತ್ ।

[Stream 2 — Northern path:] [ಸ ಏವ ಸವಿತಾ] ಉತ್ತರೇಣ [ಅಯನೇನ] ಯಾತಿ ಜ್ಞಾನಸಂಯುಕ್ತಕರ್ಮವತಾಂ ಲೋಕಾನ್ ವಿದಧತ್ ।

English: Stream 1: The Sun (and the Moon too, by upalakaṣaṇa) travels by the Southern solstice-path while distributing worlds to those who perform only ritual action.

Stream 2: That same Sun travels by the Northern solstice-path while distributing worlds to those who combine knowledge with action.

Note: The original text runs both streams together in one participial construction (ವಿದಧತ್ governing both objects). Ānandagiri's anvaya splits them explicitly and also adds that ಸವಿತಾ is an upalakaṣaṇa — it denotes the Moon as well, since the Moon too moves along these paths generating tithis.

Sentence 4 — The final statement on householder-seers and the Southern path

As written:

ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಏವಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಂ ಅನ್ನಾತ್ಮಕಂ ಫಲತ್ವೇನ ಅಭಿನಿರ್ವರ್ತಯಂತಿ ಚಂದ್ರಂ ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತ-ಕರ್ಮಣಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾರ್ಥಿನಃ ಏತೇ ಋಷಯಃ ಸ್ವರ್ಗದ್ರಷ್ಟಾರಃ ಗೃಹಸ್ಥಾಃ, ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಸ್ವಕೃತಂ ಏವ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನ-ಉಪಲಕ್ಷಿತಂ ಚಂದ್ರಂ ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

ಏತೇ ಋಷಯಃ — ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಾಃ, ಪ್ರಜಾರ್ಥಿನಃ, ಸ್ವರ್ಗದ್ರಷ್ಟಾರಃ, ಗೃಹಸ್ಥಾಃ — ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತ-ಕರ್ಮಣಾ [ಮಾಧ್ಯಮೇನ] ಅನ್ನಾತ್ಮಕಂ [ಚ] ಚಂದ್ರರೂಪಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಂ ಫಲತ್ವೇನ ಅಭಿನಿರ್ವರ್ತಯಂತಿ [ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್] — ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ [ತೇ] ಸ್ವಕೃತಂ ಏವ [ಯತ್] ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನ-ಉಪಲಕ್ಷಿತಂ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ [ಚಂದ್ರಂ] ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ ।

English: Because these seers — desirous of progeny, seekers of offspring, perceivers of heaven, householders — bring about Prajāpati in his food-natured Moon-form as their fruit through sacrificial and charitable action, therefore they resort to nothing but their own deed, which is the Southern path — the Moon indicated by the Southern solstice.

Note: The accumulation of four appositive epithets for ಋಷಯಃ and the placement of ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್…ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ across the sentence boundary makes this the densest construction in the Bhāṣya on this verse. The anvaya clarifies that ಫಲತ್ವೇನ ಅಭಿನಿರ್ವರ್ತಯಂತಿ and ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ are the two main verbs, and that ಚಂದ್ರಂ is to be supplied in the concluding clause from context.

docs.title: ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā)
docs.text:
ಸ ಮಿಥುನಮುತ್ಪಾದಯತ ಇತ್ಯುಪಕ್ರಾಂತಂ ಮಿಥುನಮುಪಸಂಹರತಿ – ಯಶ್ಚಾಸಾವಿತಿ ।

ಯಶ್ಚಾಸೌ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾ ಯಶ್ಚಾಮೂರ್ತಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಸ್ತದೇಕಂ ಮಿಥುನಂ ಸರ್ವಂ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಕಮಿತ್ಯನ್ವಯಃ ।

ಏತೌ ಮೇ ಬಹುಧಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತ ಇತ್ಯುಕ್ತಂ ತತ್ಕೇನ ಪ್ರಕಾರೇಣೇತಿ ಪೃಚ್ಛತಿ – ಕಥಮಿತಿ ।

ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣಯೋಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಾದಿದ್ವಾರಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಸ್ರಷ್ಟೃತ್ವಮಿತ್ಯಾಹ – ಉಚ್ಯತ ಇತಿ ।

ತದೇವ ಮಿಥುನಮೇವ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ ಕಾಲಃ ।

ಸ ಚ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕಮಿಥುನನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಾದಿತ್ಯಾಹ – ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಾದಿತಿ ।

ತದುಪಪಾದಯತಿ – ಚಂದ್ರೇತಿ ।

ಚಂದ್ರನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯಾಸ್ತಿಥಯ ಆದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯಾನ್ಯಹೋತ್ರಾಣೀತಿ ವಿಭಾಗಃ ।

ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವೇಽಪಿ ಕಾಲಸ್ಯ ಕಥಂ ತದಾತ್ಮಕತೇತ್ಯಾಶಂಕ್ಯ ಕಾರ್ಯಕಾರಣಯೋರಭೇದಾದಿತ್ಯಾಹ – ತದನನ್ಯತ್ವಾದಿತಿ ।

ನ ಕೇವಲಂ ತಿಥ್ಯಾದಿದ್ವಾರಾ ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ ಕಿಂ ತ್ವಯನದ್ವಯದ್ವಾರಾಽಪೀತಿ ವಕ್ತುಂ ತಸ್ಯಾಯನೇ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿವಾಕ್ಯಂ ತತ್ಪ್ರಶ್ನಪೂರ್ವಕಂ ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ – ತತ್ಕಥಮಿತಿ ।

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಂ ಕುತೋ ಹೇತ್ವಂತರಾದಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಲೋಕಾನ್ವಿದಧದ್ದಕ್ಷಿಣೇನ ಯಾತಿ ।

ಜ್ಞಾನಯುಕ್ತಕರ್ಮವತಾಂ ಲೋಕಾನ್ವಿದಧದುತ್ತರೇಣ ಯಾತೀತ್ಯನ್ವಯಃ ।

ಸವಿತೇತ್ಯುಪಲಕ್ಷಣಂ ಚಂದ್ರಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ।

ಜ್ಯೇಷ್ಠಾದಿರ್ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನಂ ಮಾರ್ಗಶೀರ್ಷಾದಿರುತ್ತರಾಯಣಮಿತಿ ಶ್ರುತಿಷು ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧೇಃ ತತಶ್ಚ ಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಲೋಕಾನ್ವಿಧಾತುಂ ತಯೋರ್ದಕ್ಷಿಣೋತ್ತರಾಭ್ಯಾಂ ಮಾರ್ಗಾಭ್ಯಾಂ ಗಮನಾತ್ತನ್ನಿಮಿತ್ತತ್ವಾಚ್ಚಾಯನದ್ವಯಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧೇಸ್ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಂ ತಯೋರಯನಯೋರಿತಿ ತದ್ದ್ವಾರಾ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಮಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯಯೋಃ ಕಥಂ ಲೋಕವಿಧಾಯಕತ್ವಮಿತಿ ಪೃಚ್ಛತಿ – ಕಥಮಿತಿ ।

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯದಕ್ಷಿಣೋತ್ತರಾಯಣದ್ವಾರಾ ಲೋಕಪ್ರಾಪ್ತೇಃ ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಲೋಕಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕತ್ವಾಚ್ಚ ತಯೋಸ್ತದ್ವಿಧಾಯಕತ್ವಮಿತಿ ತದ್ಯೇ ಹ ವಾ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿವಾಕ್ಯೇನ ಪರಿಹರತಿ – ತತ್ತತ್ರೇತಿ ।

ಇಷ್ಟಂ ಚೇತಿ ।

ಅಗ್ನಿಹೋತ್ರಂ ತಪಃ ಸತ್ಯಂ ವೇದಾನಾಂ ಚಾನುಪಾಲನಮ್ ।

ಆತಿಥ್ಯಂ ವೈಶ್ವದೇವಶ್ಚ ಇಷ್ಟಮಿತ್ಯಭಿಧೀಯತೇ ॥

ವಾಪೀಕೂಪತಡಾಗಾದಿ ದೇವತಾಯತನಾನಿ ಚ ।

ಅನ್ನಪ್ರದಾನಮಾರಾಮಃ ಪೂರ್ತಮಿತ್ಯಭಿಧೀಯತೇ ॥

ಇತಿ ತಯೋರ್ಭೇದಃ ।

ಕೃತಮಿತ್ಯುಪಾಸತ ಇತಿ ಕೃತಶಬ್ದೋಪರಿತನಮಿತಿಶಬ್ದಮಿಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತೇ ಇತಿ ಪೂರ್ತಶಬ್ದೋಪರ್ಯಾಕೃಷ್ಯಾಽಽದಿಶಬ್ದಪರ್ಯಾಯತಯಾ ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ – ಇತ್ಯಾದೀತಿ ।

ದತ್ತಮಾದಿಶಬ್ದಾರ್ಥಃ ।

ಕೃತಮೇವೋಪಾಸತೇ ಕಾರ್ಯಮೇವಾನುತಿಷ್ಠಂತೀತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಇದಂ ಚ ವಿಶೇಷಣಂ ಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತೌ ಹೇತುತಯೋಕ್ತಮ್ ।

ಕೃತರೂಪೇಷ್ಟ್ಯಾದಿಜನ್ಯತ್ವಾಚ್ಚಂದ್ರಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಕೃತತ್ವೇನಾನಿತ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ ಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತಿರಿತ್ಯಾಹ – ಕೃತರೂಪತ್ವಾದಿತಿ ।

ಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತೌ ಮಂತ್ರವಾಕ್ಯಂ ಪ್ರಮಾಣಯತಿ – ಇಮಂ ಲೋಕಮಿತಿ ॥ ೯ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Ānandagiri opens by locating this Bhāṣya passage within its context: Prajāpati was said to produce a pair (mithuna), and Śaṅkara now brings that pair to conclusion with the words "yaścāsau" (that which is the Moon). The syntax (anvaya) is: "That Moon which has form, and that Prāṇa which is formless — these two together are one pair that is everything (sarvātmaka)." It was said that "these two will produce many progeny for me" — and now the question "how?" arises.

Ānandagiri explains that Śaṅkara's answer shows how Rayi and Prāṇa, through the medium of the Saṃvatsara (Year) and related structures, become creators of progeny. That very pair (mithuna) is the Saṃvatsara — Time itself — and that Saṃvatsara is Prajāpati, because the Saṃvatsara is produced out of (nirvartyate) the pair that is of the nature of Prajāpati. Ānandagiri then unpacks the sub-point (tannirvartyatvāt): tithis (lunar days) are produced by the Moon; days and nights (ahorātras) are produced by the Sun — this is the division. Yet even though Time is produced by them, how can Time be identical to them? Ānandagiri answers by citing the principle of non-difference between cause and effect (kāryakāraṇayoḥ abhedāt) — hence "non-difference from that" (tadananyatvāt).

Ānandagiri then clarifies that it is not only through tithis etc. that the Year is produced by Moon and Sun, but also through the two ayanas (solstices) — and this is the purpose of the sub-question "tat katham?" (how so?). The real question is: from what other reason does the Year come to be produced by Moon and Sun? The correct syntactic connection (anvaya) of Śaṅkara's sentence is: the Sun travels by the Southern path while distributing worlds for those who perform only ritual action; it travels by the Northern path while distributing worlds for those who combine knowledge with action. And the word "Savitṛ" (Sun) here is an upalakaṣaṇa (indicative term) — it also implies the Moon. The Southern solstice begins with Jyeṣṭha (month), and the Northern with Mārgaśīrṣa — this is the accepted Vedic teaching. Since the two solstices are established because of the Sun (and Moon) moving along those Southern and Northern paths for the purpose of distributing worlds to the performers of action, the two ayanas are produced by them, and through the ayanas the Year too is produced by them.

To the further question "how are Moon and Sun distributors of worlds?", Ānandagiri explains: because the worlds are attained through the Southern and Northern ayanas produced by Moon and Sun, and because the worlds thus attained are themselves of the nature of Moon and Sun — therefore those two are the distributors of worlds. This is resolved by Śaṅkara's statement beginning "tad ye ha vā…" — which Ānandagiri glosses as "tat tatra."

On the definition of iṣṭa and pūrta, Ānandagiri quotes the traditional two-verse definition:

Iṣṭa is: Agnihotra, austerity (tapas), truth (satya), observance of the Vedas, hospitality (ātithya), and Vaiśvadeva rite.

Pūrta is: the digging of step-wells, wells, and tanks; construction of temples; gift of food; and planting of gardens.

On the word "kṛtam" (accomplished) — Ānandagiri explains that Śaṅkara's "iti" after "kṛtam" draws in and covers "iṣṭāpūrte" as well as "pūrta," and the word "ādi" (etc.) stands for "datta" (what is given/donated). The meaning is: they worship and carry out only what is accomplished/conditioned — only kārya (the produced, finite). This qualifier (viśeṣaṇa) is stated as the reason for their return. Finally, Ānandagiri explains "kṛtarūpatvāt": because the lunar world itself is born from conditioned acts like iṣṭi etc., it too has the character of the kṛta (the accomplished, the finite) and is therefore impermanent — hence rebirth. The Vedic statement "imaṃ lokam" is cited as the scriptural proof (māna) for this return.
